title: NAST: In-Network Aggregation with Worker Selection for Accelerating Distributed Training.
abstract: The rising scale of distributed training (DT) leads to significant communication overhead in clusters. The vast majority of communication loads are generated based on the all-reduce communication primitive. To optimize the all-reduce communication, in-network aggregation (INA) has emerged as a promising solution. Specifically, INA utilizes programmable switches to aggregate gradients within the network, thereby reducing the communication overhead. Existing DT with INA schemes primarily aggregate gradients from all workers in each iteration. However, the system environment is subject to dynamic resource competition and network congestion. As a result, the completion time of DT depends on the slowest worker, i.e., the straggler. To tackle this challenge, we propose a framework called NAST, the first-of-its-kind framework that combines INA with worker selection to accelerate DT. Specifically, we formulate the problem of INA with worker selection and theoretically analyze the convergence of NAST. Based on the convergence result, we design an efficient algorithm to dynamically determine the number of participating workers in each iteration. Then, NAST selects participants for INA based on the arrival order of workers’ gradients. We implement NAST on a testbed comprising 2 Intel Tofino switches and 9 machines. Experimental results demonstrate that NAST reduces the training time by 16.3%-29.8% and traffic consumption by 25.8%-42.4% compared to the state-of-the-art solutions.

title: FlyPS: A Flexible Multi-job Placement Scheme with Communication Scheduling in GPU Clusters.
abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence drives the deployment of massive, dedicated GPU clusters for distributed model training. However, distributed training jobs generate massive communication flows that inevitably compete for shared network links, leading to bandwidth contention. Because distributed training is highly synchronous, it is strictly bounded by the straggler effect. Even if a tiny fraction of flows experiences contention, the entire communication stage is delayed, forcing all other GPUs to stall. Existing approaches attempt to mitigate this by either enforcing strict rack-exclusive placement-which causes severe resource fragmentation-or employing dynamic traffic scheduling, which merely alleviates congestion but fails to solve the straggler problem. To bridge this gap, we propose FlyPS, a flexible job placement scheme with communication scheduling that completely eliminates bandwidth contention while maximizing resource utilization. Specifically, FlyPS first partitions the network into large contention-free domains (CFDs) based on spine switches, enabling multiple jobs to be co-located without interference. Second, for large jobs that must span multiple CFDs, it enforces a port-level isolation mechanism to prevent inter-job contention. Finally, FlyPS incorporates an edgecoloring-based scheduling algorithm to guarantee optimal intrajob communication. Testbed experiments and large-scale simulations demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art schemes, FlyPS successfully eliminates all bandwidth contention and reduces job iteration time by up to 49.5%.

title: Scylla: Scheduling Multiple Latency-Sensitive Applications in the Edge-Cloud Continuum.
abstract: Cloud-hosted applications can experience significant latency, particularly for users located far from data centers. Edge computing mitigates these issues by distributing processing across geographically distributed locations. However, the limited resources at edge sites must be carefully allocated across applications to avoid contention that would outweigh the benefits of lower network latency. We present Scylla, a multi-application, latency-aware scheduler for edge/cloud environments. Scylla accurately predicts the relationship between resource allocation and tail latency using a queuing model faithful to the load distribution mechanisms used in Kubernetes. It then computes a global scheduling plan for multiple applications that ensures the respect of tail latency objectives, while minimizing the volume or cost of necessary edge resources. We evaluate Scylla on real-world infrastructure using Kubernetes and several latency-sensitive applications, including edge AI workloads. Our results show that Scylla effectively predicts tail latencies and makes scheduling decisions that utilize just the right amount of resources with low computational overhead, in contrast to state-of-the-art schedulers used in the industry or proposed in earlier research.

title: Janus: Edge Content Negotiation for Agent-Oriented Web QoS.
abstract: LLM agents increasingly retrieve web content through tool calls, yet current web delivery paths remain optimized for human browsing rather than machine reasoning. A typical page carries layout, scripts, image assets, and boilerplate that increase network transfer and context tokens without improving an agent’s task state. Janus reframes agent-web optimization as an explicit edge content-negotiation problem: agents opt into machine-oriented representations, while ordinary users continue to receive original pages. The gateway generates, validates, and caches compact semantic variants at the provider or CDN edge, and passes through unsupported content unchanged. Preliminary read-heavy workloads show up to 40.1% task-time reduction, 62.4% context-token reduction, and over 70% fetched-volume reduction for browser-driven agents.

title: Achieving Fast and High Throughput Data Exchange for Serverless Computing Systems via Switch-Native Serialization/Deserialization.
abstract: Serverless computing has emerged as a dominant cloud paradigm that enhances development efficiency and reduces operational costs. Serialization and deserialization are key operations in these systems. However, these processes may contribute up to 98% of the total latency, making the host compute-bound. Recent serialization-free approaches, such as RMMap, eliminate serialization overhead by directly mapping memory between functions in distributed serverless systems. Nevertheless, transferring raw memory produces large payloads and imposes significant network demands, rendering the process bandwidth-bound. To address these challenges, we propose HyperLink, a networkassisted system that unifies the benefits of both compute-bound and bandwidth-bound approaches. HyperLink offloads intensive serialization tasks (e.g., data compression) to programmable switches, while the host employs a lightweight memory mapping mechanism. It features a parallel striped storage module for efficient compression dictionary management, a latency-aware adaptive encoder that balances compression delays with compression ratios, and a dependency-gated parallel decoder that decouples packet-level decoding into block-level processing to enhance throughput. Experimental results show that HyperLink reduces latency by up to $\mathbf{6 8. 1 2 \%}$ and achieves $\mathbf{8. 2 5} \times$ throughput compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

title: It Takes Two: Embracing Sparsity and Speculative Decoding for Efficient LLM Inference.
abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) has emerged as a promis-ing approach to accelerate large language models (LLMs) in-ference.Yet, this acceleration comes at the cost of a higher memory footprint. Sparse activation (SA), on the other hand, has demonstrated effectiveness in reducing memory footprint in LLM inference. Despite the apparent synergy between these twomethods, we find that a straightforward combination actually undermines the benefits of both, due to a fundamental conflict in their optimization objectives. The conflict arises because speculative decoding accelerates token generation by verifying multiple tokens in parallel, which inevitably activates more weights within an autoregressive step, thus undermining the benefits of sparsity. In this paper, we present SpaDec, a novel speculative decoding framework to resolve this conflict and achieve more efficient LLM inference. To achieve this goal, we introduce a light-weight draft-token acceptance predictor module, coupled with an acceptance-guided tree selection algorithm that leverages the target model’s initial hidden layer featuresto proactively trim tokens that are unlikely to be accepted during token verifica-tion. This process introduces minimum extra latency but leaves sparse activation algorithm ample space to minimize redundant computations while maintaining the high accuracy essential for speculative decoding, ultimately achieving both inference speedup and memory footprint reduction brought by speculative decoding and sparse activation, respectively. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate that SpaDec achieves up to 4.31$\times$ speedup while saving an additional 30.0% – 35.3% of memory, which outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) solutions by 30.7% – 44.25% on average.

title: The Enduring Potential of Locality: Efficient Routing for Fine-Grained Cluster Deduplication.
abstract: Data routing is a critical step in cluster deduplication, as it aggregates redundant data chunks onto the same nodes to eliminate redundancy. Previous researches focused on identifying and aggregating exactly duplicate chunks, while overlooking similar but non-identical chunks, which leads to significant compression loss. The challenge arises from the high overhead in searching for the node containing the most similar chunks, which is vastly more expensive than detecting exact duplicates using simple fingerprint matches. To this end, we propose GPRoute, which aggregates both identical and similar chunks while reducing routing overhead through two strategies. ① The fuzzy search strategy leverages inter-chunk locality to reduce search breadth, by simplifying multiple fine-grained routing decisions for several contiguous chunks into a single coarse-grained routing decision. ② The global speculation strategy exploits spatial locality to reduce search depth, by speculating routing decisions on the client side using historical information prefetched from servers. To our knowledge, GPRoute is the first routing method that enables similarity-aware chunk aggregation with practical overhead. Our results show that GPRoute achieves up to $4 \times$ reduction in the storage size compared to previous coarse-grained stateless routing method while maintaining comparable routing overhead.

title: Taming GPU Inference Variability with Risk-Aware Scheduling and Dynamic Kernel Segments.
abstract: The growing divergence between GPU hardware capabilities and the phasic, variable nature of deep learning inferencecreates a critical scheduling challenge. Existing schedul-ing strategies fail to address the gap, leading to severe queuing delays and increased interference sensitivity. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a novel scheduling paradigm centered on a dynamic granularity abstraction, the Kernel Segment (KS). KS is an intelligent scheduling unit that, through offline profiling, intrinsically encapsulates compute-stall phase behavior. We exploit a lightweight interference prediction model that uniquely decouples a task’s inherent resource sensitivity from contention pressure. Then, the Risk-Aware Spatio-Temporal Scheduling (RASTS) algorithm is proposed, which decomposes the problem into synergistic control planes. RASTS dynamically modulates KS granularity based on real-time latency risk while proactively optimizing spatial resource allocation to minimize contention. Extensive evaluation across CNN and LLM bench-marks demonstrates that RASTS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, improving utility by 67%, reducing latency inflation by 44%, anddecreasing SLO violations by 62%.

title: Odysseus: A Context-Level Pre-training Framework for Out-of-Distribution Encrypted Traffic Classification.
abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is essential for network security, management, and Quality of Service (QoS), but models trained under IID assumptions often degrade after deployment due to application updates, temporal drift, and infrastructural changes. We observe that short-window multi-flow context provides more stable behavioral cues than isolated flows, while self-supervised pre-training can learn transferable priors from unlabeled traffic without target-domain labels. We present Odysseus, a context-level pre-training framework for OOD encrypted traffic classification. Odysseus converts raw pcaps into a Multi-Scale Flow Grid Representation (MSFGR) and pre-trains a masked autoencoder with complementary packet- and flow-level masking to capture intra-/inter-flow structure. During fine-tuning, it integrates Hierarchical Attention Distillation (HAD), Traffic-Aware Augmentation and Contrastive Learning (TACL), and Associated Flow Prediction (AFP) to enhance context modeling, distill context knowledge into a deployable flow-level branch, and regularize OOD-robust relational representations. Across 11 scenarios (5 IID, 6 OOD) spanning Cross-Version, Cross-Time, Cross-Spatiotemporal, and Cross-Type shifts, Odysseus achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves OOD F1-Score by up to $15.70\%$, reaching $85.38\%$, $90.05\%$, $71.93\%$, and $99.62/96.87/72.55\%$ F1 on the corresponding OOD settings. Further analyses confirm the effectiveness of each component, strong few-shot robustness, graceful degradation under noisy/missing context, and advantages over matrix-based inputs.

title: FedQCab: A Common Plug-and-Play Layer-wise Quantization Tool for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed edge devices while preserving data privacy. However, severe communication overhead remains a primary bottleneck, especially in resource-constrained and heterogeneous environments. Existing quantization methods typically rely on uniform compression or rigid heuristics, which often overlook the varying learning behaviors across network layers and the dynamic bandwidth budget, inevitably sacrificing model accuracy for communication efficiency. To resolve these challenges, we propose FedQCab, a generic and plug-and-play layer-wise quantization tool designed to minimize communication overhead without compromising model performance. FedQCab introduces a lightweight hypernetwork to formulate an adaptive quantization policy. By leveraging a Differentiable Quantization Policy Generation mechanism via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, we transform discrete bit-width selection into a differentiable training process to support hypernetwork training. Furthermore, FedQCab employs a bandwidth-constrained and task-aware optimization that directly minimizes the actual task loss while strictly adhering to real-time client bandwidth budgets. This feedback mechanism allows the system to intelligently allocate limited bit resources to sensitive layers while aggressively compressing robust layers. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets and architectures demonstrate that FedQCab significantly outperforms baselines, achieving up to 31.8% accuracy improvement and reducing communication overhead by up to 9.59× under dynamic bandwidth constraints.

title: CodedFRER: Enhancing Reliability for FRER Protocol via Erasure Codes in Error-Prone Networks.
abstract: Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) is a protocol designed for high reliability with low latency in Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) by transmitting replicated frames over redundant paths. However, we find that FRER’s replication-based redundancy strategy leads to critical reliability challenges in error-prone networks, where high error rates may cause the correlated loss of all replicas for a single frame (we term correlated all-replica loss). Additionally, FRER eliminates redundant frames at path intersections to avoid duplicate delivery, raising the risk of correlated all-replica loss. Existing work on improving FRER’s reliability mainly focuses on optimizing routing and scheduling to reduce the eliminations at path intersections, yet fails to tolerate correlated all-replica loss. In this paper, we propose CodedFRER, an erasure-codingbased FRER architecture that transmits coded parity frames over selected paths to handle correlated all-replica loss and achieve high reliability in error-prone networks. We also propose two methods to reduce decoding overhead and optimize original and parity frame paths. Experiments show that CodedFRER improves Quality of Service (QoS) by 42.49% in error-prone networks, while reducing end-to-end delay by $\mathbf{2 2. 6 7 \%}$ and network traffic by 27.18%, compared to the state-of-the-art strategy.

title: Privacy-aware Hand Gesture Recognition using Textile-based Sensing Glove.
abstract: Gesture recognition using a wearable sensor glove enables intuitive human-robot interaction, virtual reality, and rehabilitation systems; however, hand motion patterns and finger configurations are highly user-specific and may reveal sensitive biometric information. To address this issue, this study implements a federated learning-based gesture recognition framework utilizing a textile-based sensing glove. In this study, multichannel signals from five finger sensors embedded in the glove were processed. A lightweight Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) temporal model was employed, and two federated learning strategies, Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and Federated Representation (FedRep), were implemented. Using centralized training, the model achieved accuracies of 99.78% and 75.87% under random split and Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) evaluation, whereas using federated training, accuracies of 99.81% and 75.06% were obtained, respectively. As a result, it has been shown that federated learning preserves recognition performance with only a slight reduction in accuracy while providing improved data privacy. The findings demonstrate that combining temporal modeling with personalized federated learning enables privacyaware and low-latency gesture recognition suitable for real-time applications.

title: Renewables Power the Orbit? Achieving Sustainable Space Edge Computing via QoS-Aware Offloading.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are becoming integral to 6G infrastructure, but increasing in-orbit computation accelerates battery degradation and raises sustainability concerns. Meanwhile, renewable-heavy regions worldwide experience persistent energy curtailment due to transmission bottlenecks, leaving substantial clean energy stranded near generation sites. We identify a satellite-grid co-design opportunity: adaptively offloading task-critical data from satellite to data centers co-located with renewable power plants. However, realizing this vision requires jointly considering intermittent and capacity-limited communication windows, as well as time-varying electricity budgets. In this paper, we propose SQSO, a Sustainable and QoS-aware Satellite Offloading framework that models per-interval task offloading as a constrained optimization over dynamic topology and electricity prices. Under this framework, we design $\text{AO}^2$, an adaptive offloading orchestration algorithm to solve the formulated optimization problem. Using Starlink-scale simulations and real-world electricity price traces, $\text{AO}^2$ reduces energy consumption by up to 76.03% and battery life consumption by up to 76.85% compared to state-of-the-art schemes, while also lowering task delay. This work highlights that sustainable scaling of LEO constellations requires co-design of space networking and renewable energy infrastructure, while our solution promotes renewable-aware task offloading and cross-domain collaboration for space-energy integration in the 6G era.

title: WiFi-based Human Pose Estimation via Intermediate Pose Synthesis and Part Grouping.
abstract: As a non-contact and privacy-friendly sensing technology, WiFi-based human pose estimation holds significant potential for applications in intelligent surveillance and humancomputer interaction. However, existing methods still face two critical challenges. First, temporal sparsity caused by crossmodal alignment. To match low-sampling-rate visual labels, high-sampling-rate CSI signals are forced to be downsampled, leading to the loss of intermediate motion information. Second, the “negative transfer” effect caused by global feature sharing. Most models adopt a global feature sharing strategy, ignoring the relative independence of different body parts in motion patterns, which introduces interference from irrelevant parts and limits the precise modeling of highly dynamic joints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel WiFi-based pose estimation framework that integrates temporal-interim pose synthesis with part-wise grouping modeling. In the temporal dimension, we design a temporally aware pose synthesis module that follows a “coarse-to-fine” generation strategy, explicitly inferring intermediate poses between adjacent frames in the feature space, thereby substantially enhancing temporal continuity. In the structural dimension, we introduce a data-driven part grouping strategy based on mutual information to automatically discover correlations among body parts, and employ a multi-branch network to model each part group independently, which mitigates negative transfer and strengthens local feature representations. Extensive experiments on the WiPose and MM-Fi datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under the strict PCK@10 metric, achieving notable improvements especially on highly dynamic joints such as wrists and ankles. These results validate the effectiveness of our approach in continuous motion modeling and fine-grained WiFi-based pose estimation.

title: QoS-driven Network Soft Slicing through Token-based Hierarchical Scheduling.
abstract: Today’s network applications require strict Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees, specifically regarding latency and bandwidth. Network soft slicing is an effective method to satisfy these per-service QoS requirements on shared physical infrastructures, which logically divides a physical network into virtual slices, allocating specific bandwidth to each slice to support individual services. A major challenge with existing soft slicing methods is interference between slices. Typically, a slice is classified as underload when its packet transmission rate remains within its allocated bandwidth, and overload when it exceeds this limit. If traffic from both slice types shares a network device, overload slices might consume bandwidth allocated to underload slices. This interference causes severe queueing delays and violates the QoS agreements of the underload slices. To solve this interference and maintain QoS, we propose a lightweight, practically-deployable scheduler called Token-based Hierarchical Traffic Scheduler (THTS) to ensure traffic isolation and reliable delay performance. The essence of THTS is a lightweight operation that jointly monitors packet accumulation and bandwidth usage to accurately detect overload slices. Using the state identification, our hierarchical scheduling architecture efficiently gives transmission priority to underload slices, and thus minimizes interference and keeps queueing delays low. To analyze the performance of THTS, we derive theoretical upper bounds on queueing delays for underload slices. Simulation results indicate that THTS lowers the average steadystate delay by 67% and decreases storage requirements by over 80% relative to existing solutions. Furthermore, our analytical method increases the accuracy of delay upper bound estimation by up to 95% compared to current industrial practices.

title: Noah: Tile-Level Interval Analysis for NPU Performance Modeling.
abstract: To meet the large-scale tensor computation requirements of LLMs, NPUs have become a mainstream architecture. Understanding their performance characteristics requires tools that can accurately capture complex hardware behaviors. However, existing approaches are limited by a trade-off: simulations enable accurate analysis but incur substantial cost, while analytical models offer speed but are too abstract to describe resource contention. To overcome these challenges, we propose Noah, a novel NPU analytical model. Noah models NPUs with a custom AI accelerator command ISA and reconstructs kernel execution as a pipelined interaction among compute, memory, and communication components. To improve fidelity, we explicitly model overlap behavior and major runtime stalls. For complex microarchitectural effects that are difficult to describe analytically, Noah incorporates a lightweight neural network. The proposed framework aims to provide an efficient and extensible approach for NPU performance modeling and early-stage design exploration.

title: SpecNet-Agent: Network-Aware Speculation Control for QoS in Agentic Generative AI Services.
abstract: Agentic generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) services increasingly process user requests as dynamic workflows that combine planning, retrieval, tool use, code execution, judging, and summarization, creating dependency-sensitive network transfers rather than a single model call. Existing quality of service (QoS) mechanisms are insufficient because flow scheduling, tenant fairness, static priorities, and coflow abstractions cannot reliably separate workflow-blocking traffic from cancelable or quality-elastic speculative branches. This paper presents SpecNetAgent, a runtime-network feedback framework that collects workflow hints, classifies traffic by probabilistic criticality, monitors congestion telemetry, and applies a safeguarded contextual-bandit controller to adjust retrieval width, agent parallelism, speculation budget, and background synchronization before traffic enters deployable QoS queues. The evaluation uses replay inputs derived from real-world agent execution logs, covering 1,237 workflows across retrieval-augmented generation question answering (RAG-QA), coding-agent, research-agent, and multi-agent debate templates under light, medium, and heavy loads. Under heavy load, SpecNet-Agent reduces p99 workflow latency to 192.93 time units, improving by 94.3% over first-in, firstout (FIFO), 89.9% over static priority, and 24.7% over criticalpath-only scheduling. It lowers deadline misses to 1.0% and cuts wasted speculative bytes by 76.2% over FIFO. Unlike aggressive rule-based feedback, it preserves a retained-speculation quality proxy of 0.967. These results demonstrate a practical contribution: network-aware source-side speculation control for improving QoS in agentic GenAI services.

title: Learning from Experience: Real-time and Efficient Network Measurement on Programmable Switches.
abstract: Sketches are one of the most efficient methods for network measurement. Some learning-based methods have addressed the issue of traditional sketches relying on a single assumption. However, due to the complexity of learning-based models, they can only be deployed on resource-rich servers. This necessitates frequent communication with the server when-ever the switch requires specific statistical information, thereby failing to satisfy the real-time decision-making requirements. Furthermore, the inability to obtain prior information in realtime hinders the execution of more complex downstream tasks. In this paper, we propose LFE, which simplifies the operations of learning-based models, making them compatible with programmable switches. LFE ensures the transmission of information within the switch, thereby supporting more complex realtime tasks. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that after optimization by LFE, the five commonly used sketches achieve an average reduction in AAE by 13.83% and an average reduction in ARE by 14.67%, with only a 4.56% reduction in throughput. The implementation is available at the repository1.

title: Structure-Aware GPU Scheduling with Cycle Fusion and Feedback Adaptation for Multi-Task Training.
abstract: Deep learning training workloads exhibit a highly iterative execution pattern, where GPU computation phases (forward/backward propagation) and idle phases (data loading, synchronization) strictly alternate. Existing GPU schedulers, operating at coarse task granularity, are oblivious to this intrinsic structure, leading to frequent GPU idling during iteration boundaries and task switches, ultimately degrading resource utilization and system throughput. This paper proposes a structure-aware GPU scheduling optimization for multi-task training. Our approach integrates three core mechanisms: online iteration structure recognition enabling accelerated task switching; a scaling model for fused execution that derives feasible concurrency ranges and constructs cycle-aligned fusion windows to co-schedule multiple tasks, filling idle phases with complementary computation; and adaptive feedback-driven control that dynamically modulates scheduling intensity based on real-time kernel arrival ratios. Experimental results show that our approach improves GPU utilization by $\mathbf{3 2 - 4 7 \%}$ and achieves $\mathbf{1. 2 2} \times \mathbf{- 1. 4 6} \times$ throughput gains over exclusive execution, while outperforming existing sharing strategies by 5-25% across diverse workload combinations.

title: Multi-View Flow Representation and Relation Graph Modeling for Network Traffic Classification.
abstract: The widespread deployment of encryption protocols has fundamentally reduced payload visibility in network traffic, posing significant challenges to network behavior inference systems (e.g. Network Intrusion Detection System, NIDS) based solely on packet contents. Existing approaches often depend on coarse-grained flow-level statistics or isolated protocol metadata, which limits their ability to capture fine-grained TCP/IP packet sequences within individual flows as well as interaction patterns across multiple flows. From passive traffic measurements, we observe that an encrypted client–server communication typically spans multiple protocol stages, including domain name resolution, TLS handshake, and encrypted payload transmission. Additionally, complex network behaviors are often manifested through a sequence of correlated five-tuple flows rather than a single flow. To address these challenges, we propose a robust network behavior modeling framework, MV-FlowGraph, which characterizes encrypted traffic by jointly modeling multi-view intra-flow features and temporal inter-flow dependencies. Specifically, MV-FlowGraph consists of three key components: (1) a flow-level feature extraction and representation module that leverages server-side domain features recovered from plaintext DNS traffic, TLS handshake metadata, and TCP/IP packet transmission sequences; (2) a flow relation graph module that builds application-level flow graphs to capture inter-flow concurrency and sequential dependencies; and (3) a multi-view fusion module that employs BERT, autoencoders, and Graph Attention Networks to jointly model multi-view intra-flow features and temporal inter-flow features. Extensive experimental results verify that MV-FlowGraph out-performs state-of-the-art methods (e.g., AppScanner, FS-Net, and FG-Net) in detecting network anomalies targeting online services.

title: ISP or Customer? Inferring the Ownership of Public IPs of Non-Cooperative Satellite Internet via Internet Measurements.
abstract: The rapid development of Starlink has spurred extensive measurement studies in recent years. Early research predominantly employed “in-outside” measurement methods. Owing to their potential for low cost and broad coverage, “outside-in” approaches have recently gained increasing attention. These methods require the use of public IP addresses assigned to Starlink users in order to effectively measure the system. However, research on the mechanisms behind Starlink’s public IP address assignment remains limited. We investigate the identification of ownership for publicly routable Starlink IP addresses and propose a novel latency-based approach, LatencyScope, to distinguish between customer devices and ISP ground infrastructures. Through systematic latency measurements and multi-perspective experimental validation, our method enables accurate inference of the ownership of publicly routable Starlink IP addresses. Our method is applicable to other Low Earth Orbit satellite networks for IP attribution. With LatencyScope, we conduct a large-scale measurement of Starlink. For IPv4, we identify distinct address prefixes and assignment patterns for customer devices and ground infrastructures. For IPv6, we employ two target generation algorithms to efficiently discover approximately 3.4 million active addresses, substantially expanding the available dataset, uncovering assignment patterns, and correcting misclassifications in existing works. The findings provide a comprehensive view of Starlink’s IP addressing architecture.

title: TD-RCA: Topology-Aware and Dual-Perspective Decoupling for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices.
abstract: The widespread adoption of microservice architectures improves the agility and scalability of modern software systems, but complex service dependencies make failure diagnosis increasingly difficult. Root cause analysis (RCA) aims to identify the source service responsible for a failure from heterogeneous observability signals. Existing correlation-based or graph-based methods often assume complete distributed traces and unidirectional anomaly propagation. In production, network loss can remove call edges from the observed trace topology, leading to Structural Invisibility. In addition, synchronous blocking Remote Procedure Call (RPC) can amplify upstream anomaly signals and cause Cascade Confusion, where victim services exhibit stronger symptoms than the true root cause. To address these challenges, we propose TD-RCA, an unsupervised topology-aware RCA framework with dual-perspective decoupling. TD-RCA builds on a multi-modal VAE-GNN reconstruction model: it separately encodes trace-side execution signals and metric-side resource loads, and adaptively fuses them at the representation level. Reconstruction deviations of node and edge attributes serve as base anomaly signals. To handle Structural Invisibility, a Topology-Aware Detection (TAD) module discovers common topology modes in an unsupervised manner and infers missing call edges to produce a structural anomaly signal. To mitigate Cascade Confusion, a Dual-Perspective Decoupling (DPD) module models incoming pressure and outgoing propagation from callee and caller perspectives to distinguish root causes from cascaded victims. Experiments on two public benchmark datasets (TrainTicket and SocialNetwork) show that TD-RCA achieves HR@1 of 93.9% and 94.3%, respectively, and remains effective under incomplete traces and complex cascading failures.

title: MAS-CP: Multi-Agent Communication Prediction for Distributed Deep Neural Network Training.
abstract: Predicting all-reduce communication latency in distributed deep neural network (DNN) training is challenging because latency depends on both shared network state and per-worker program behavior. Existing approaches rely on monolithic predictors with fixed architectures, making them brittle across models and cluster sizes. We propose MAS-CP, a multi-agent framework with Locator, Analyzer, Predictor, and Verifier agents plus an orchestrator and RAG memory. On realworld BERT/GPT-2 traces and simulated multi-worker clusters with worker counts $W=2,4,8,16$, MAS-CP reduces MAE by $\mathbf{3. 6 \% - 6. 1 \%}$ over the best fixed-configuration baselines, with a closed-loop verification mechanism that automatically triggers re-prediction when errors exceed a dynamic threshold.

title: NeuroForensics: Unmasking Covert Backdoor Attack via Endogenous Defense.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates decentralized training without exchanging raw data, yet remains inherently susceptible to backdoor attacks. Existing defenses predominantly rely on statistical outlier detection, assumed that malicious updates exhibit significant deviations from benign ones. However, this premise is fundamentally flawed in real-world scenarios, particularly against covert backdoor attacks within non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data conditions. In this paper, we propose a robust FL defense framework, called NeuroForensics, that employs a target-oriented approach to resist covert backdoor attacks under Non-IID data characteristics. To uncover endogenous anomalies, we project high-dimensional model weights into a Posterior Probability Matrix via Pseudo Feature Vectors (PFV). This projection helps magnify the endogenous divergences between malicious and benign clients. Furthermore, to characterize these disparities across multiple dimensions, we incorporate a multi-metric fusion strategy that synthesizes matrix features into a unified anomaly detection score, enabling an adaptive thresholding mechanism to accurately isolate malicious clients. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that NeuroForensics significantly outperforms existing defense schemes, suppressing backdoor success rates while preserving high main-task utility, even under covert attacks and extreme Non-IID conditions.

title: Chariot: Accelerating Distributed Protocols with Data-Path Accelerator in DPUs.
abstract: Distributed protocols such as Paxos are fundamental to achieving high reliability and strong consistency in modern distributed systems. However, widely deployed implementations suffer from substantial data-path overhead, especially when built on the standard kernel networking stack. Programmable Data-Path Accelerators (DPAs) in modern DPUs offer new opportunities to accelerate data-path processing for distributed protocols, but effectively offloading such processing remains challenging due to hardware constraints and software complexity. We present Chariot, a set of DPA-based optimizations for distributed protocols. First, Chariot introduces a DPA-based broadcast mechanism that encapsulates data-path complexity behind simple APIs and offloads message transmission to the DPA, exploiting parallel execution to accelerate broadcasting. Second, Chariot provides a DPA-based quorum confirmation mechanism that selectively intercepts acknowledgment packets and performs quorum confirmation on the DPA, reducing hostside processing overhead. Our evaluation shows that Chariot improves the throughput of a classic Multi-Paxos replication protocol by up to $2.2 \times$. Index Terms-Data-Path Accelerator, Distributed Protocols

title: Later is More: Trading Tolerable Latency to Meet Stringent Jitter Requirement in Time-Sensitive Networking.
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) has become a key infrastructure for latency-sensitive industrial applications. However, the massive number of industrial devices inevitably experience uncertain delay variations in packet generation and transmission, leading to deviation between the arrival times at the switch. These deviations spread hop by hop and eventually increase the risk of violating latency jitter bounds. To address this issue, this paper proposes Adaptive Delay for Jitter (Adjer), a dynamic mechanism that actively defers packet transmissions at switches to reduce the deviation between the packet arrival times, while still meeting the end-to-end latency constraints. Through theoretical analysis, we deduce the minimum deferring time to meet the jitter bound. The comprehensive test results of testbeds and simulations demonstrate that Adjer significantly improves the success ratio compared with state-of-the-art approaches while satisfying end-to-end latency and jitter constraints.

title: Heterogeneous Tasks Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing: A Federated Meta Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) enables latency-sensitive vehicular applications by offloading computation-intensive tasks to nearby edge servers. However, real-world vehicular workloads are typically modeled as heterogeneous directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks with complex dependency structures, making joint offloading and resource allocation highly challenging. Moreover, distributed MEC deployment raises privacy concerns when collaboratively training learning-based policies. In this paper, we propose a Federated Meta Deep Reinforcement Learning framework with GAT-Seq2Seq modeling (FedMAGS) for heterogeneous task offloading in VEC systems. The proposed approach leverages Graph Attention Networks to capture DAG dependencies, a Seq2Seq-based policy to generate structured offloading decisions, and federated meta-learning to enable fast adaptation across distributed MEC servers without sharing raw data. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FedMAGS achieves faster convergence, lower execution delay, and better scalability compared with state-of-the-art baselines. In addition, the federated design preserves data privacy while reducing communication overhead, making the framework well suited for dynamic and large-scale VEC environments.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: TAILOR: Token-Aware Partitioning and Routing for Edge-Cloud Transformer Inference.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in collaborative edge–cloud environments to reduce latency and cloud cost. However, autoregressive transformer inference exhibits strong token-level variability: output lengths are unknown at request arrival, KV-cache memory grows during decoding, and long-tailed requests can trigger out-of-memory (OOM) failures on memory-constrained edge devices. Existing static partitioning methods collapse this token-dependent cost surface into a single layer-to-device mapping, which either underutilizes edge resources or causes high-latency cloud fallback for long outputs. This paper presents TAILOR, a token-aware inference framework that jointly optimizes offline partitioning and online routing for autoregressive transformer serving. TAILOR builds token-length buckets, generates memory-feasible partitioning strategies along the latency–memory trade-off frontier, selects a compact subset under edge capacity constraints, and routes each request according to predicted output length and device availability. Experiments with GPT-2 models on a heterogeneous edge–cloud testbed show that TAILOR reduces end-to-end latency by up to $22.2 \%$, improves throughput by up to 28.5%, and lowers OOM-induced fallback by up to 73.1% compared with static partitioning baselines, demonstrating robust inference under long-tailed token workloads.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: REACT: Toward Real-Time, End-to-End, Adaptive Cross-Layer Restoration for IP-Over-Optical Networks.
abstract: The resilience of optical networks is challenged by frequent fiber cuts. Jointly optimizing optical-layer rerouting and IP-layer traffic allocation yields optimal recovery, but solving the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is prohibitively slow for real-time operation. Precomputation-based frameworks address this by generating recovery plans for highprobability failure scenarios, yet the number of possible failure patterns grows exponentially with network size, leaving numerous unforeseen cases unprotected. Recently, ML-based optical-layer restoration techniques are introduced to handle missed scenarios, but IP-layer recovery remains a bottleneck, limiting real-time responsiveness. To bridge this gap, this paper presents REACT, a responsive learning framework that enables real-time, joint optical and IP-layer restoration. REACT operates through two tightlyintegrated components: (i) an optical-layer restoration module that employs Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to swiftly generate feasible Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) plans, and (ii) an IP-layer recovery module built upon a two-stage architecture: an initial traffic generation layer that transfers the network features into preliminary allocations, and a self-correction adjustment layer that refines these allocations using network metrics generated by the initial allocation. Evaluations on real-world topologies demonstrate that REACT achieves 95–99% of the optimal restoration throughput while delivering a speedup of over 19–3761$\times$ compared with other state-of-the-art (SOTA) cross-layer restoration schemes.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Dynamic Malicious Encrypted Traffic Detection via Temporal Knowledge Graph in Cloud-Edge Networks.
abstract: Traditional centralized security is inadequate for Cloud-Edge Networks, where massive distributed traffic and widespread protocol encryption create severe security blind spots. Continuous monitoring of network traffic is essential to identify malicious encrypted activities such as lateral movement and zero-day attacks. Existing graph-based detection methods typically model network flows as static graphs, which fail to capture the temporal dynamics of traffic patterns and face severe scalability bottlenecks when processing massive streaming data at resource-constrained edge nodes. Furthermore, supervised models heavily rely on exhaustive labeled datasets that are impractical to maintain in highly dynamic environments. To address these limitations, we propose TKG-ETA, a self-supervised Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) neural network equipped with an adaptive sketch mechanism for dynamic Encrypted Traffic Analysis in cloud-edge networks. We utilize a dynamically configurable sketch algorithm to efficiently compress and extract multi-dimensional statistical features from massive streaming traffic with minimal memory overhead, entirely bypassing payload inspection. These features are continuously transformed into a lightweight streaming TKG to model the fine-grained communication relations among network entities over time. Based on this temporal structure, we design a self-supervised time-aware message-passing mechanism to autonomously learn the evolutionary trajectories of normal encrypted traffic patterns without manual annotations. By capturing structural and temporal deviations, the proposed model accurately identifies malicious encrypted traffic. Extensive experiments on real-world network traffic datasets demonstrate that TKG-ETA achieves superior detection accuracy with an weighted F1 score exceeding 96% while maintaining the high throughput and low resource overhead imperative for cloud-edge collaborative deployment.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: A Flexible-Topology Rack-Scale Interconnect Architecture for Heterogeneous LLM Workloads.
abstract: In this paper, we present a flexible-topology rack-scale interconnect architecture for large language model (LLM) workloads. Unlike conventional rack designs that hard-bind a single scale-up topology, our approach decouples interconnect topology from rack cabling and compute trays through filed-swappable interconnect trays. By replacing only the central trays, a rack can be reconfigured between a switch-based full-rack fabric and multiple low-latency point-to-point clusters. The proposed retimer-based bridge tray significantly reduces interconnect hop latency—from 900ns in switch-based designs to 30n, while also lowering tray-level cost and power consumption. This enables a single rack platform to efficiently serve both bandwidth-intensive workloads and latency-sensitive workloads. We describe practical lane mappings that realize 8 $\times$ 8 and 4 $\times$ 16 full-mesh clusters from 1 $\times$ 64 full-rack without recabling. Our results indicate that flexible interconnect trays provide a cost-effective and low-latency alternative to fixedtopology rack-scale interconnects.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RABR-Co: Retention-Guided SVC ABR with Joint Buffer Tuning for Non-linear Video Streaming.
abstract: Interactive video users exhibit frequent non-linear actions (e.g., seeking, skipping, and early departure), breaking the sequential-consumption assumption of conventional Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) streaming and causing substantial bandwidth waste due to prefetching. In Scalable Video Coding (SVC) streaming, progressive buffering further exacerbates this problem. Later segments naturally receive more enhancement-layer data, yet they are statistically more likely to be skipped, resulting in systematic over-allocation to late segments and a severe resource-utility mismatch. To address these challenges, this paper presents RABR-Co, a retention-guided joint framework that couples SVC-ABR decisions with coordinated buffer tuning. RABR-Co converts historical user-derived retention curves into segment-level playback probabilities and importance weights, and uses them to jointly optimize enhancement-layer selection, prefetching depth, and buffer occupancy. High-retention segments are prioritized for quality upgrades and stable delivery, while skip-prone regions are fetched conservatively to reduce waste and recover quickly from seek-induced buffer disruptions. RABR-Co is evaluated in a Mininet-based emulation with real-world network traces and interactive viewing models. Results show that RABR-Co reduces wasted traffic while improving effective bitrate utilization and Quality of Experience (QoE) in frequently watched regions, with more stable playback.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: GaLB: Gap-Aware Load Balancing for High-Performance AI Training in RDMA Networks.
abstract: In modern AI training clusters, efficient load balancing is essential to achieve low-latency and high-throughput communication. Although advanced flowlet-based methods in Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) datacenter networks are widely adopted for preventing out-of-order packets, they inadvertently harm performance by misinterpreting all interpacket gaps (IPGs) as congestion, triggering unnecessary and disruptive rerouting. To address this issue, we present a gapaware load balancing mechanism (GaLB), which proactively identifies non-congested IPGs to prevent unnecessary rerouting. Specifically, GaLB leverages both IPG measurements and flow control frame states to discern the nature of inter-packet gaps, enabling differentiated routing strategies. Experimental results show that GaLB significantly outperforms state-of-theart schemes, reducing the average and the $99^{t h}$ percentile flow completion times (FCT) by 21.4% and 22.3%, respectively, while lowering the out-of-order event rate by 25.3%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Toward Communication-Sensing Integrated Cloud-Network Monitoring: Real-Time Vibration Event Recognition on Underground Optical Cables.
abstract: Underground optical cables are key assets in cloudnetwork infrastructure, and distributed optical fiber sensing enables them to serve as both communication media and sensing resources for external disturbance monitoring. This paper presents a real-time vibration event recognition framework for communication-sensing integrated underground opticalcable monitoring based on $\Phi$-OTDR signals. To avoid temporal information leakage, continuous vibration traces are divided into non-overlapping training, validation, and testing periods before sliding-window segmentation and Z-score standardization. The proposed SE-DMRCB model integrates parallel multiscale 1D convolutions, stacked residual blocks, and squeezeand-excitation attention to capture both impulsive and periodic vibration patterns. Bayesian optimization is employed to select key hyperparameters for balancing recognition accuracy and model complexity. Experiments on a real-world underground optical-cable deployment with eight vibration-event categories show that the proposed method achieves 99.84% test accuracy with an end-to-end recognition latency of 10.55 ms per window, which is much lower than the 512 ms window-update interval. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can support online recognition and sensing-assisted diagnosis for cloud-network infrastructure operation.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RCAgentBench: An Agent-Oriented Benchmark for Multimodal Root Cause Analysis in Microservices.
abstract: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is pivotal for ensuring the reliability of microservice systems. Traditional RCA approaches are often limited by the scarcity of labeled data and insufficient interpretability. Recently, Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents have emerged as a promising direction for automated RCA, thanks to their broad knowledge, strong reasoning, and orchestration capabilities. However, the absence of diverse labeled datasets, standardized tools, and systematic assessment of agent patterns hinders the rigorous evaluation of RCA agents. To address these issues, we propose RCAgentBench, the first agent-oriented benchmark tailored for microservice RCA. First, we construct a multimodal RCA dataset, covering metrics, logs, and traces, and manually annotate each case with reasoning keywords to enable comprehensive evaluation of agent performance. Second, we introduce standardized tools and agent patterns to support reproducible evaluation and decouple tool capabilities from agent reasoning power. Finally, we explore different experimental settings across a diverse spectrum of LLMs, spanning from small-scale open-source models to frontier closed-source models, and provide actionable insights for the future design of RCA agents. All evaluation framework code has been made publicly available at: https://github.com/CSTCloudOps/RCAgentBench.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: H2I: A Handover-State Encoding-Based Data Inheritance Method for Mobile Crowdsensing.
abstract: In mobile crowdsensing (MCS), participants often drop out, requiring their unfinished tasks to be migrated to othersa process known as task migration. However, existing work rarely addresses how to properly handle the residual data from exiting participants, leading to low data utilization and degraded quality, which harms MCS Quality of Service (QoS). To tackle this, we propose H2I, a data inheritance method based on handover-state encoding. H2I first introduces a hierarchical data quality assessment framework: a point-level layer uses taskembedded multi-head attention to estimate collection quality for each record, while a grid-level layer employs an Attention U-Net to assess credibility using spatial context. These scores jointly guide data correction. We find that quality assessment alone cannot distinguish natural variations caused by task migration from true anomalies, often causing over-smoothing. To solve this, H2I incorporates handover-state encoding, which models the spatiotemporal proximity and historical observation states of the exiting participant and the successor. A gated fusion mechanism then uses this encoding to control the direction and scale of correction. Extensive simulations show that H2I outperforms existing methods in MAE, $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$, and other metrics, significantly improving data quality during task migration.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Temporal Predictive Joint Hybrid Beamforming Framework for Mitigating Channel Aging in High-Mobility MIMO-OFDM Systems.
abstract: As a key technology for enhancing spectral efficiency, Frequency Division Duplexing (FDD) massive multipleinput multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) is limited by channel aging in high-mobility scenarios. The latency in channel estimation and feedback renders Base Station (BS) CSI outdated relative to rapid channel variations caused by Doppler shifts, leading to beam misalignment. To combat the issue, we propose a unified framework called Predictive Attention-aided Multi-Scale Hybrid Beamforming (PAMS-HBF). The architecture integrates a Learnable Pilot Sensing (LPS) module for adaptive downlink pilot design, functioning for both downlink pilot transmission and user-side pilot sensing, alongside a Long Short-Term Channel Prediction (LSTCP) module using LSTM to forecast CSI for aging compensation. A Multi-Scale CSI Feedback (MCF) module employs multi-scale convolutions to capture diverse features for compression. An Efficient Channel Attention Beamforming (ECAB) module at the BS reconstructs features to generate beamforming matrices. Experimental results demonstrate that PAMS-HBF maintains consistent performance across different velocities. Comparisons show its superiority over traditional algorithms and static deep learning schemes. The proposed method at sufficient feedback bits exceeds the lossless feedback baseline by approximately 23.1%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: HeraClass: Towards Open-World Network Flow Classification via Traffic-Language Mapping.
abstract: Network traffic classification in open-world settings, where applications evolve dynamically and labeled data is limited, remains an important unsolved problem. Existing techniques designed for static closed-world scenarios struggle when faced with shifting traffic patterns and categories. In this work, we formulate open-world flow classification (OWFC) as a crossmodal translation problem and identify four key challenges: (1) bridging the modality gap between traffic data and class labels, (2) discovering novel unknown classes at run-time, (3) learning representations for complex traffic features, and (4) rapidly adapting to new environments. To address these challenges, we propose HeraClass, a novel OWFC system that models temporal and categorical traffic features separately and learns them automatically, and maps traffic to a semantic language space to align known flows and their class labels, while making unknown flows depart from known class labels and thus maintaining low confidence to identify them as known ones. HeraClass supports real-time classification and can efficiently adapt to new environments using low-rank adaptation. Testbed experiments demonstrate HeraClass’s strong performance on both standard benchmarks and open-world scenarios, outperforming state-ofthe-art baselines by $\mathbf{1 2 0. 1 0 \%}$ on average for OWFC. We opensource pre-trained models, datasets, and implementation code to facilitate future research1.

title: Mitigating Cold Starts in Container-Ephemeral Large Language Model Serving.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in serverless environments to enable elastic and costefficient inference. Existing LLM serving systems primarily optimize steady-state throughput under persistent GPU workers with long-lived model residency. In contrast, container-ephemeral deployments provision isolated instances on demand, causing high cold start latency during scale up events. In this paper, we present FaLLServe, a framework for container-ephemeral LLM serving in serverless environments. Our key insight is that the high cold start latency is dominated by the local deployment phase, particularly workflow overhead and tensor copy during model loading. FaLLServe introduces an initless model loading mechanism, an advanced container workflow, and a multi-level prewarm scheduler to reduce both cold start latency and its frequency. Experimental results show that FaLLServe reduces cold start latency by up to 49.$\times$ and improves tail latency by up to 270.3$\times$ under real-world workloads, making latency-critical LLM inference practical in ephemeral serving environments.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CANListener: A Lightweight and Adaptive Intrusion Detection System for In-vehicle CAN Bus.
abstract: Controller Area Network (CAN) bus is the core communication backbone in modern vehicles, responsible for connecting Electronic Control Units (ECUs) and coordinating real-time in-vehicle operations. However, it is intrinsically without built-in security mechanisms. Existing works proposed Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) to protect CAN bus, ranging from rulebased to machine learning and deep learning-based methods. But most of them either require significant labeled samples or computational resources, or they suffer from severe detection performance degradation. Toward this end, this paper proposes CANListener, a lightweight and adaptive IDS for in-vehicle CAN bus. CANListener first employs a Reinforced Active Learning (RAL)-based method to train detection models with minimal but valuable labeled samples, enabling label-effective but accurate learning. Then, it integrates a Reinforcement Learning (RL)gated two-stage framework to dynamically allocate computational resources by routing inputs between lightweight and deep expert ensembles. Experimental results on real automotive datasets demonstrate that CANListener can achieve strong detection performance (99.48% TPR, 0.01% FPR) using only 1% labeled data, while maintaining real-time detection with an average CPU usage of 4.5% under hardware deployment.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CDWF: Few-Shot Learning for Cross-Domain Multi-Tab Website Fingerprinting.
abstract: Website fingerprinting attacks allow an eavesdropper to determine which websites a user is visiting by analyzing metadata from encrypted traffic, thereby posing a significant threat to online privacy. Most current methods rely on the assumption that a user visits only a single webpage at a time, which fails to account for the prevalence of multi-tab browsing in realistic scenarios. In such environments, traffic from multiple websites is interleaved, and practical attacks are further hindered by the scarcity of target-domain data, which limits the training efficacy and generalization of conventional models. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CDWF, a cross-domain few-shot website fingerprinting framework for multi-tab settings. The framework utilizes a three-stage progressive learning pipeline. First, traffic-augmented pre-training on public datasets extracts generalizable traffic representations through contrastive learning with diverse packet-level perturbations. Next, adversarial domain adaptation to align feature distributions between the source and target domains. Finally, few-shot target adaptation using a minimal set of target-domain samples and their augmented versions for rapid deployment. Experimental results demonstrate that CDWF significantly outperforms existing baselines in closed-world, open-world, and various defense scenarios. CDWF maintains superior robustness and recognition accuracy even when the number of tabs is unknown and under strong defensive conditions. This work provides an effective solution for practical website fingerprinting attacks in environments with limited data and constrained resources.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Beyond Up and Down: Analyzing Temporal Phenomena in IPv6 Probing Responses.
abstract: IPv6 address responsiveness exhibits pronounced temporal dynamics that remain poorly characterized: prior work largely focuses on IPv4 or static IPv6 snapshots, leaving longitudinal behavior and its implications for anomaly detection and Internet-scale modeling largely unexplored. We present a scalable active-measurement framework that constructs a routabilityfiltered, density-prioritized target set, conducts synchronized hourly multi-vantage probing with conservative-then-convergent labeling, and applies STL decomposition to separate longterm trend, recurring seasonality, and transient disturbances in block-level time series. Applied to 5,000,000 IPv6 addresses over 100 days, the framework reveals a strongly polarized survival structure, a sustained decline in aggregate daily survival overlaid with robust diurnal and weaker weekend periodicity, and systematic stratified differences across /64 subnets, IIDgeneration types, and countries. These findings demonstrate that IPv6 responsiveness forms structured, decomposable phenomena, providing a foundation for anomaly detection and persistent address characterization in Internet-wide measurement.

title: MACH: A Matrix-Accelerated Classifier for High-throughput Packet Processing on GPUs.
abstract: Packet classification is a core function in modern network systems. While learning-based methods demonstrate promising throughput on large-scale rulesets, existing indices fail to effectively exploit GPU parallelism. Specifically, the hierarchical structure of recursive models creates irregular control flow patterns, leading to branch divergence and non-coalesced memory accesses that degrade throughput at scale. To address this limitation, we propose MACH, a throughput-oriented packet classification framework. MACH utilizes a unified neural network trained on multi-dimensional features to ensure complete rule coverage without rule duplication. By adopting a semi-structured design that couples the neural model with a tuple space, the framework reduces model complexity and supports efficient dynamic updates. Crucially, this architecture transforms irregular rule lookups into dense matrix operations, aligning classification tasks with GPU computation primitives. A CPU-GPU hybrid streaming pipeline is further implemented to maximize aggregate batch throughput. Evaluations on rulesets with 512k entries demonstrate that MACH achieves 12.19x and 9.37x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art learning-based baselines, NuevoMatch and NeuTree, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: BEP: A Bayesian-Entropy Pruning Framework for Efficient IPv6 Active Network Discovery.
abstract: Efficient discovery of active IPv6 subnets is critical for network measurement and security analysis, yet the 2128address space renders exhaustive scanning infeasible. Existing approaches fall into two categories, both fundamentally mismatched with the subnet discovery problem: target generation algorithms rely on seed-address clustering patterns absent in ISPallocated subnets, while hitlist-seeded methods are structurally confined to already-measured network regions. We introduce BEP, a Bayesian-Entropy Pruning framework that unifies all exploration decisions under a single statistical quantity—the posterior estimate of the prefix activity rate $p_{v}$—defined as the expected fraction of /64 subnets within a prefix that are active—derived from expected loss minimization over the prefix hierarchy. BEP requires no seed addresses, handles sparse and absent evidence within the same Beta-distributed posterior update, and propagates hierarchical priors with strength proportional to accumulated evidence. Deployed across 386,247 /32 prefixes spanning 84,029 autonomous systems from three geographically distributed vantage points (San Francisco, Frankfurt, and Tokyo), BEP discovers 149.8 million active /64 subnets—4.7$\times$ more than the best-performing adapted TGA baseline and $10.5 \times$ more than hitlist-seeded inference— with 94.7% reachability confirmed via traceroute. Ablation analysis confirms that principled Bayesian estimation accounts for the majority of this gain, with hierarchical prior propagation and uncertainty-adjusted pruning providing additional systematic improvements.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Adaptive Multi-Path Mamba Knowledge Distillation Framework for Industrial Defect Detection.
abstract: Industrial defect detection (IDD) plays a vital role in intelligent manufacturing. In practical industrial environments, defects are often small-scale, low-contrast, and morphologically complex, posing stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. Real-time edge deployment demands a careful balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency; however, existing methods remain constrained by the inherent accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. To address this challenge, we propose a deployment-oriented Multi-Path Mamba-in-Mamba Knowledge Distillation framework (MPMiM-KD), designed to preserve strong detection capability while minimizing inference overhead. Specifically, a multi-path Mamba teacher network is constructed to capture multi-scale defect patterns through parallel branches with diverse receptive fields, providing enriched supervisory signals during training. The teacher model is used exclusively for knowledge transfer and does not increase deployment complexity. An adaptive distillation strategy with dynamic temperature control is further introduced to efficiently transfer discriminative knowledge to a compact student network. In addition, cross-path attention enables intermediate feature alignment, enhancing robustness to complex defect patterns without incurring additional inference cost. Experimental results on the Real-IAD dataset demonstrate that MPMiM-KD improves AUROC by 2.4% over the previous state-of-the-art while reducing model parameters by 30.3% and computational cost by 17.7%, indicating its potential for efficient industrial defect detection under resource-constrained deployment scenarios.

title: Exploring Energy Saving Opportunities for Data Center Cooling Systems.
abstract: Cooling systems are a major source of electricity consumption in data centers. Existing studies mainly focus on device-level and unit-level optimization, with limited attention to coordinated energy saving across multiple cooling units and buildings. This paper proposes a hierarchical optimization method for data center cooling systems, covering single-unit optimization, multi-unit coordinated operation, and multi-building ordinated optimization. Under cooling demand and operational constraints, the method is evaluated across year-round operating conditions. Results show that, compared with existing unit-level optimization methods, the proposed method improves overall energy saving performance by $\mathbf{2 0. 8 6 \%}$.
