title: Tremerity-Fi: Non-Contact Daily-Life Tremor Severity Assessment by Commercial mmWave Radar.
abstract: Tremor is a common symptom of neurological diseases. The regular assessment of daily tremors facilitates the evaluation of disease progression and assists clinicians in optimizing treatment strategies. However, current home monitoring solutions have difficulty in dealing with user cooperation, privacy concerns, environmental interference, and system generalization, leading to feasibility concerns in activities of daily living (ADL). To this end, we propose Tremerity-Fi, a non-contact and privacy-friendly tremor severity assessment system based on mmWave radar. To realize Tremerity-Fi, we first design an adaptive beamforming algorithm to accurately identify useful but weak signals from numerous reflections captured in the environment. Second, unlike primary reflections commonly used in mmWave sensing, we leverage multipath reflections that carry useful information about the target's motion, even though they are generally considered harmful, to help reconstruct hand signals and improve sensing performance. Furthermore, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation algorithm to improve the ability to adapt to unseen environments and users. We collect a diverse dataset of 5 patients and 25 healthy subjects in 3 scenarios, such as offices, homes, and hospitals. Extensive experiments show that our system achieves 94.51% accuracy in tremor detection, about 5 higher than the SOTA mmWave radar method, and 89.13% in tremor severity assessment, demonstrating its sufficient potential as a tremor monitoring assistant for patients with neurological diseases.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Pluto: Fast and Accurate Persistent Flow Detection in High-Speed Networks via Adaptive Protection.
abstract: In modern networks such as IoT and data center environments, massive volumes of data flows are continuously generated, making real-time traffic monitoring essential for maintaining reliability and detecting anomalies. Among these flows, persistent flows, those that recur over extended periods, are particularly important, as they capture long-term traffic behaviors that can reveal stealthy network anomalies. Detecting such flows, however, is challenging due to high traffic rates and limited memory resources. Approximate data structures, such as sketches, are commonly used for network traffic measurement, but efficiently deploying them on emerging programmable switches remains nontrivial. These switches provide line-rate packet processing and flexible programmability, yet impose strict hardware constraints, such as limited computational operations and pipeline stages. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel hardware-friendly sketch, Pluto, specifically designed for programmable switches to enable accurate and resource-efficient persistent flow detection in high-speed networks. We provide a formal analysis to establish its theoretical soundness and prototype Pluto on CPU, FPGA, and industry-grade Tofino switches. Extensive evaluation on real-world traces demonstrates that Pluto achieves high detection accuracy while incurring limited resource overhead.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RiCE: Precise Remote In-Network Congestion Elimination in Inter-Datacenter RDMA Networks.
abstract: High-performance distributed applications, such as Large Language Model (LLM) training and real-time database synchronization, increasingly span geo-distributed datacenters (DCs), demanding sustained inter-DC high throughput. While RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCEv2) offers high performance within local fabrics, extending its lossless abstraction to long-haul inter-DC networks is challenging. Propagating Priority Flow Control (PFC) across high-latency inter-DC links risks triggering widespread deadlocks and congestion spreading. Standard congestion control mechanisms (e.g., DCQCN) fail in this setting due to the excessive feedback delay imposed by the large Round-Trip Time (RTT). In this paper, we propose RiCE, a novel inter-DC congestion control framework designed to achieve sub-RTT reaction, scalable granularity, and robustness to feedback staleness, while remaining transparent to end-hosts. RiCE employs a split-loop architecture to decouple local and remote congestion handling. For local congestion, the sender’s DCI gateway generates immediate feedback to throttle traffic before buffers overflow. For remote congestion, RiCE deploys a transparent proxy at the remote DCI gateway that enforces rate limiting on a per-path granularity. By exploiting the deterministic downward routing of Clos topologies to aggregate flows sharing the same physical bottleneck, RiCE emulates per-flow fairness without requiring prohibitive per-flow queues. Complementing this, a Remote Feedback Filter masks transient noise to prevent premature throttling. We implemented a DPDK-based prototype and conducted extensive evaluations on a physical testbed and large-scale simulations. Results show that RiCE achieves up to 3.3$\times$ the throughput of DCQCN and reduces flow completion time by up to 50% compared to state-of-the-art solutions.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Ygg: Tree-Based Collaborative Speculative Decoding with Token-Only Transmission.
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable performance, the QoS for the LLM inference system is still constrained by the substantial latency inherent in autoregressive decoding. To accelerate the decoding process, speculative decoding has recently been proposed, employing both a lightweight draft model and the target LLM residing in the cloud to rapidly generate candidate tokens and verify these candidates in parallel, enabling the processing of multiple tokens per step. However, co-deploying the draft and target models in the cloud wastes valuable GPU memory resources and limits the cloud’s ability to perform parallel inferences for higher throughput. To further improve inference QoS by achieving higher throughput, in this paper, we propose Ygg to offload the draft model onto the cost-effective edge device, relieving the computational workload of the cloud in collaborative manners. To address the drawback of excessive data transmission in existing speculative decoding methods, we design a novel collaborative paradigm with tokenonly transmission, which drastically cuts down communication latency. Furthermore, Ygg incorporates two additional key designs: budget-aware adaptive tree-based draft generation and asynchronous pipelining, which serve to elevate the acceptance rate of generated draft tokens and boost inference throughput, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves up to 1.94× throughput improvement and reduces serving costs by 47.3% compared to the cloud-only speculative decoding method. Furthermore, in comparison with the state-of-the-art edge-cloud collaborative method, Ygg reduces the overall inference latency by up to 49.3% and consistently achieves the best performance across diverse tasks and varying LLM scales.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: P4XC: A Unified Compiler Framework for Network Dataplane with Heterogeneous Processors.
abstract: Driven by the need to meet stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements, programmable dataplane architectures are evolving from homogeneous processors to heterogeneous hybrid ones that combine pipelines and RTC cores. However, corresponding programming frameworks lag behind, particularly for emerging flexible hybrid architectures. The lack of a unified abstraction makes it challenging to optimize resource allocation for the service level agreement (SLA) guaranty. To address the challenges, we propose P4X, which extends P4 as a unified language to support RTC semantics as well, ensuring consistent processing logic across heterogeneous units. Furthermore, we design the compiler framework, P4XC, which automates task partitioning to maximize worst-case throughput and optimize mapping based on strict performance objectives. We validate the solution by implementing multiple forwarding and in-network computing applications on fixed and flexible hybrid architectures. Experimental results show that P4XC is adaptive to different targets and significantly outperforms manual expertise in achieving superior QoS metrics. P4XC provides a solid foundation for supporting the continuous evolution of performance-critical programmable dataplanes.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: BGP-Shadow: Accelerating BGP Verification via Programmable Data Planes.
abstract: BGP configurations are complex and error-prone, posing a major threat to the stability of large-scale networks. Existing control-plane verification approaches largely fall into two categories: monolithic verifiers, which suffer from statespace explosion and scale poorly, and modular verifiers, which require manual decomposition of global properties into local invariants and are therefore tedious and error-prone. To address these challenges, we present BGP-Shadow, a high-performance framework for BGP configuration verification built on programmable data planes. BGP-Shadow compiles network-wide BGP configurations and policies into P4 match-action table entries, and introduces topology folding to emulate hop-by-hop BGP route propagation over a logical topology via iterative in-switch packet recirculation. This design enables invariantfree automated verification, eliminating the need for manual modular decomposition or handcrafted formal invariants, while maintaining efficiency and scalability. Experimental results show that BGP-Shadow reduces verification time by 60% compared to Timepiece and can effectively support configuration assurance for production-scale networks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Velo-NC: Verified Worst-Case End-to-End Queueing-Delay Bounds Under Network Dynamics.
abstract: Modern networks must provide stringent Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees for time-sensitive applications despite failures, traffic shifts, and BGP dynamics. Control-plane verifiers such as Velo can explore these uncertainties and compute the worst-case link loads, but do not yield time-domain end-toend queueing-delay bounds; conversely, Network Calculus (NC) provides such bounds but typically relies on static traffic envelopes, i.e., arrival curves, that ignore routing dynamics. We present Velo-NC, a framework that bridges these approaches by translating Velo’s worst-case link-load envelopes into conservative residual service curves and end-to-end deterministic queueingdelay bounds under an explicit steady-state traffic and scheduling abstraction. We additionally study an optional subtraction-based tightening and validate it empirically. Beyond the steady-state core, Velo-NC supports optional stochastic and transient extensions that provide probabilistic risk estimates and convergenceaware assessments under user-chosen convergence, stochastictraffic calibration, and threat models. We implement Velo-NC in Rust and evaluate it on Internet Topology Zoo networks, showing that it computes the verified worst-case queueing/virtualdelay bounds quickly (tens of milliseconds on median in our runnable subset, with a heavy tail under multi-failure stress tests). When deterministic guarantees are feasible under the stated model, Velo-NC returns finite bounds while explicitly accounting for failures and BGP uncertainty. Its distinguishing feature relative to heuristic or simulation-percentile baselines is verification over the modeled uncertainty space. Overall, Velo-NC enables practical configuration validation and capacity planning with formally grounded guarantees within the stated models.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ALCHEMY: Reusing Congestion Control Wisdom for Adaptive QUIC Transport.
abstract: No single congestion control (CC) algorithm performs well across heterogeneous and time-varying network conditions. While loss-based, delay-based, and hybrid designs excel in specific regimes, they degrade outside them. Conversely, fully learned CC approaches offer adaptability but raise concerns regarding interpretability and deployment safety. Consequently, today’s systems lack a robust mechanism to dynamically select the optimal strategy during an active connection. We address this gap with ALCHEMY, a framework that enables adaptive CC selection in QUIC. ALCHEMY introduces a state-preserving midstream switching mechanism that allows CC algorithms to be safely changed within an ongoing connection without triggering slow-start resets or control instability. Building on this capability, ALCHEMY employs an offline-trained deep reinforcement learning policy to select the most appropriate expert algorithm at runtime using cross-layer transport signals. Rather than replacing existing CC logic, ALCHEMY orchestrates established heuristics, leveraging their complementary strengths. Implemented in a high-fidelity emulated QUIC stack and evaluated across 26 diverse network scenarios, ALCHEMY demonstrates superior adaptability compared to static baselines. It improves the scenario-wise winning rate by approximately 29% relative to the best-performing individual heuristic CC algorithm. Here, winning rate denotes the frequency of achieving the highest composite throughput–delay score among all evaluated schemes. Unlike static algorithms that are bound to a fixed design envelope, ALCHEMY consistently maintains near-optimal throughput-delay trade-offs across heterogeneous and volatile regimes.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ISP-Path Alignment Can Outweigh Protocol: An HTTP/3 Case Study in Suzhou, China.
abstract: We compared HTTP/3 (QUIC) and HTTP/2 (TCP) on same-ISP and cross-ISP paths in a single-deployment Suzhou–Ningbo, China case study with multi-ISP, multi-protocol, and multi-size factorial measurements. On matched same-ISP paths, HTTP/3 delivered its expected time-to-first-byte (TTFB) advantage while maintaining high large-payload success rates. On the cross-ISP path from China Mobile (Mob) to China Telecom (Tel) under a short interactive client deadline, 20MB HTTP/3 success dropped to $24\%$ (vs. $70\%$ for HTTP/2); failures were deadline-bound mid-transfer stalls, not handshake or TLS errors. A linear-progress upper bound separated two cross-ISP regimes: a Mob→Tel deficit that largely closed under a longer deadline, and a Tel→Mob collapse that persisted for both protocols.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: LocMore: Locating More Bursty Latency-critical Jobs on Resource-constrained Nodes.
abstract: Modern cloud platforms struggle to efficiently colocate bursty latency-critical (LC) services because peak traffic can exceed average load by an order of magnitude and saturate a server’s capacity, forcing providers to dedicate at least one physical node per job to prevent QoS violations. Existing reactive schedulers are too slow for microsecond-scale spikes and cannot handle simultaneous bursts that exceed single-node capacity. We propose LocMore, a resource-efficient scheduler that breaks the one-job-per-node barrier. LocMore aggressively colocates bursty LC jobs whose combined peak demands exceed a single node’s capacity. Instead of relying on reactive reallocation, LocMore clones each LC job across distinct nodes and returns the earliest response. By proactively reserving shared headroom and intelligently steering traffic, LocMore ensures at least one clone of every job remains fully provisioned. Our evaluation demonstrates that LocMore achieves a $\mathbf{1. 5} \times$ improvement in LC density while strictly maintaining over 99% QoS compliance and eliminating simultaneous burst violations.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: HawkEye: Hierarchical Intent Inference for Critical Targets on Edge-Cloud Co-Assisted UAVs.
abstract: Urban safety inspection by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires accurate and trustworthy recognition of target intent, yet existing efforts face a dual dilemma: the system level struggles to handle limited UAV arithmetic and high cloud transmission latency, and the algorithmic level is susceptible to trajectory noise and unreliable “black-box” decisions. To this end, we propose HawkEye, a data-model dual-driven two-stage intent inference framework. Adopting an edge-cloud collaboration paradigm, HawkEye handles UAV observations with two innovative breakthroughs. On the edge, to overcome the uncertainty of target motion, we replace traditional single-trajectory fitting strategies with an anchor-based statistical inference method for short-term intents. By fusing anchor classification with kinematic constraints and Bayesian-optimized adaptive fault-tolerant intervals, this method predicts physically feasible and noise-robust steering angles and trajectories within milliseconds, providing solid priors for the cloud. On the cloud, we tailor the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for long-term tactical-level intents. A domain knowledge base embedded with typical motion and interaction features is especially built, empowering Large Language Models (LLMs) to make high-accuracy, map-free, and logically traceable intent inference. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that HawkEye improves short-term accuracy to 88.5% with 61.5% latency reduction, and long-term accuracy by 19.4%, successfully balancing real-time response and reliable intent recognition.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ChatGosen: A Network Configuration Synthesis Approach with Semantic-Computation Decoupling.
abstract: Network configuration synthesis aims to translate high-level configuration intent into concrete device-level configurations. Recent research has explored leveraging large language models (LLMs) for intent inference and configuration synthesis. However, configuration synthesis inherently requires deterministic topology analysis and protocol-parameter resolution, such as deriving OSPF link costs, BGP route preferences, or static-route next hops from topology constraints and intended forwarding behavior. These operations require explicit protocol semantics and cannot be reliably guaranteed by the probabilistic generation process of LLMs. We propose ChatGosen, a network configuration synthesis method based on semantic-computation decoupling. This approach separates intent inference from deterministic protocol-parameter resolution through a structured, vendor-independent intermediate representation (IR). The LLM handles intent reasoning, task decomposition, generation of device-level configuration subtasks, and final configuration file generation, while topology parsing and protocol-parameter resolution are processed by a deterministic protocol-parameter resolution module. We implemented a prototype system supporting static routing, OSPF, and BGP protocols. Testing on the Topology Zoo real-world network topology dataset demonstrated ChatGosen achieves fully correct routing forwarding configurations in single-intent scenarios across 64-router topologies, with accuracy exceeding 85% in multi-intent scenarios. The synthesis process completes in mere minutes, proving that semantic-computation decoupling provides a practical and scalable foundation for network-wide configuration synthesis.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: FedPDR: Server-Side Post-Plateau Refinement for Federated Learning with Latent Diffusion.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has gained prominence for its ability to enable collaborative model training while preserving data privacy in distributed environments. Despite its potential, two critical challenges persist. First, non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data across clients induce severe parameter divergence, which conventional linear aggregation fails to reconcile, leading to suboptimal convergence. Second, FL often encounters a performance plateau where frequent client-server synchronization yields diminishing returns. While existing adaptive communication schemes attempt to mitigate this, they often struggle to balance the optimal model accuracy with the stringent resource constraints of edge devices. To address these challenges, we propose FedPDR, a two-stage server-side optimization framework designed to improve both efficiency and convergence in FL. An adaptive plateau detection mechanism is employed to determine the onset of the post-optimization stage. Once a performance plateau is identified, the refinement tasks are offloaded to the server, eliminating further client involvement and mitigating post-plateau inefficiencies. Central to this approach is the use of a latent diffusion model to capture the distribution of global model parameters and generate optimized updates, thereby alleviating suboptimal convergence caused by data heterogeneity. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks and real-world settings demonstrate that FedPDR effectively shifts computational burdens, reduces client-side overhead, and consistently improves global model performance while maintaining broad compatibility with existing FL frameworks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: GBNN: In-Network Gradient Boosting Neural Network.
abstract: In-network intelligence offloads machine learning models to programmable network devices for line-rate packet classification and improved quality of service (QoS). However, existing lightweight models are often limited in fine-grained classification, while Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs), though accurate for complex traffic classification tasks, are difficult to deploy in network due to resource constraints, sequential inference latency, and disruptive runtime updates. To address these challenges, we propose GBNN, an in-network GBDTequivalent model that replaces GBDT leaf nodes with Binary Neural Networks (BNNs). GBNN preserves the boosting structure of GBDTs while leveraging compact bitwise BNN inference to reduce resource consumption and latency. Moreover, its BNNbased design enables a shadow model mechanism for nondisruptive runtime updates without device reboot. Experiments on a Raspberry Pi-based testbed show that GBNN achieves accuracy comparable to GBDT, while reducing CPU usage by 82.5% and inference latency by over $7.1 \times$.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Decentralized But Not Immune: Empirical and Formal Security Analysis of Messaging Networks.
abstract: As decentralized messaging networks (DMNs) evolve, there is an increasing need for automated methods to systematically profile their ecosystems and formally verify the security of their underlying protocols. In this study, we propose a modular and automated framework, D-MAP, that combines large-scale data collection with formal security verification, enabling the abstraction, modeling, and analysis of security protocols across diverse DMN platforms. Leveraging D-MAP, we perform empirical measurements and protocol-level verification across several representative DMNs (namely, Matrix, Berty, Jami, and Status). Our analysis uncovers a range of security issues spanning both network infrastructure and protocol layers, including DMNs node IP address exposure (4.4% of 78K DMN nodes), software supply chain weaknesses, and cryptographic flaws in handshake and encryption protocol that permit man-in-the-middle and impersonation attacks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ConvexLens: Overcoming Frequency Stagnation in Millisecond Workloads via Temporal Co-location.
abstract: Serverless and edge computing have shifted cloudnative workloads toward millisecond-scale fragmentation, exposing a fundamental hardware-software mismatch. We identify a critical bottleneck termed Frequency Stagnation, where CPU cores are trapped in low-frequency states because task execution windows are shorter than the frequency transition latency. Existing macro-autoscalers (HPA/VPA) focus solely on quota provisioning, remaining fundamentally blind to this millisecondlevel inertia. To bridge this gap, we propose ConvexLens, a non-intrusive container scheduling framework. Unlike traditional schedulers, ConvexLens leverages a perception-aware Micro-level Co-location mechanism. It aggregates scattered execution fragments into continuous high-load windows, effectively driving the hardware to lock cores at high-frequency states. Architecturally, a dual-layer Global-Local design decouples millisecond-level local agility from global resource fairness. Extensive evaluations using workloads derived from Azure production traces demonstrate that ConvexLens mitigates Frequency Stagnation, reduces P99 latency SLO violations by an order of magnitude, and decreases CPU resource consumption by up to 53.79%. Crucially, it breaks the traditional trade-off between performance and efficiency, delivering near-optimal QoS without the energy penalties of static governors.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Desi: Revisiting Signature Verification in Blockchain-based Storage System.
abstract: Blockchain-based storage systems are fundamentally limited in write throughput due to the computational overhead of signature verification during consensus. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose Desi, a novel framework that optimizes write transaction processing. In Desi, storage nodes remove individual signatures from incoming write requests and cache the simplified transactions. Once a batch reaches a predefined target condition, a Merkle tree is constructed over the batch, and the root hash is signed to form a root transaction that participates in consensus. To guarantee timely and accurate query results, storage nodes can combine cached write information with on-chain data, preventing delayed writes from affecting reads. To defend against potential malicious behavior by storage nodes, Desi incorporates a challenge-and-response mechanism, enabling verifiable accountability and user compensation. Experimental results demonstrate that Desi achieves 2.8–3.8x higher write throughput compared to the baseline mechanism, while maintaining security and verifiability.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Cloud-Compatible and Scalable Private Messaging via Authentication Piggybacking.
abstract: Private information retrieval (PIR)-based private messaging provides protection for communication metadata (e.g., conversation counterparts, timing, and frequency), yet it inherently suffers from prohibitive server-side computational costs. Recent work alleviates this scalability bottleneck at scale by adopting a distributed architecture that offloads intensive PIR computation to requesting clients. However, this strategy necessitates continuous contributions from the requesting clients, contradicting the cloud paradigm of computational offloading. In this paper, we propose an authentication-embedded PIR scheme dubbed AuEPIR. By piggybacking PIR computation into the login handshake, AuEPIR offloads server-side computation to authenticating clients without introducing additional interactions. Furthermore, we leverage AuEPIR to build a metadata-protecting communication system, called AuMPCS, which achieves cloud-compatible and scalable private messaging. Experimental results on our prototype implementation show that AuMPCS achieves second-level response latency and millisecond-level authentication latency in large-scale deployments, which significantly reduces computation delay compared with existing centralized approaches. As a result, we effectively harness the aggregated resources of idle clients to amplify system throughput. This approach simultaneously preserves security and quality of service (QoS), offering a viable solution for private messaging.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Joint Optimization of Video Recommendation and Cooperative Edge Caching for Maximizing Profit.
abstract: The rapid growth of multi-version video-on-demand (VoD) services places increasing pressure on mobile networks. Edge caching offers a promising solution by bringing content closer to mobile users (MUs). However, practical edge caching systems face a fundamental challenge: MUs exhibit highly varied preferences across video contents and bitrates, whereas edge resources are limited, costly, and influenced by pricing decisions from mobile network operators (MNOs). In this paper, we study a novel, profit-oriented joint optimization problem that integrates personalized video recommendation, cooperative multi-version edge caching, soft cache hits, and economic incentives. We model the interaction between the MNO and the video provider (VP) as a Stackelberg game, which explicitly captures the coupling between pricing decisions, caching strategies, and various demands of MUs. We also show that the studied problem is NP-hard due to its non-convex structure and the presence of mixed discrete-continuous decision variables. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Backward-Induction Stackelberg framework, in which the MNO optimizes cache-leasing prices via an iterative distance-weighted strategy, while the VP solves its NP-hard joint decision problem through block coordinate descent combined with relaxation-and-rounding techniques. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art schemes, improving the MNO’s revenue by up to 32.18% and the VP’s revenue by up to 33.43%, while remaining robust under diverse system configurations.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ReMu: Bridging Fidelity and Flexibility in High-Mobility Network Emulation at Microsecond Scale.
abstract: Emulating high-mobility networks presents a fundamental trade-off between fidelity and flexibility. While existing software methods prioritizing flexibility lack performance fidelity, hardware-based approaches conversely suffer from limited flexibility. In this paper, we propose ReMu, which achieves scalable network emulation by interconnecting software nodes via dynamic links with an architecture of offloading data plane emulation to an FPGA NIC. ReMu utilizes match-action tables to dynamically assign link models and parameters to each packet, and schedules these packets using multi-level calendar queues for precise link emulation. Experimental results on Xilinx UltraScale U250 FPGA demonstrate that ReMu achieves delay control with standard deviation below $4.5 \mu \mathrm{~s}$, loss rate error around 0.35%, and complete flow isolation even with $1 \mu \mathbf{s}$ delay differences. Furthermore, ReMu reduces link model system calls by up to $6 \times$ compared to software emulators while supporting dynamic link reconfiguration during emulation.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: AdaMoA: Enhancing Mixture-of-Agents via Task-Adaptive Architecture Optimization.
abstract: As the scaling of single LLMs encounters diminishing returns, ensembling multiple LLMs has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing model capabilities. Mixture of Agents (MoA) has shown a particular effectiveness ensemble method by leveraging the complementary strengths of diverse LLMs through multi-layer collaboration. However, current MoA architecture employs multiple layers with all agents activated at each layer, which results in dense agent invocations and introduces redundant information, leading to token inefficiency and compromised output quality. In this paper, we propose AdaMoA, a task-adaptive architecture optimization framework that enhances MoA along two dimensions: vertical layer depth and horizontal agent composition. AdaMoA determines the sufficient number of layers based on task complexity and only retains agents with task-specific expertise, therefore achieving both improved efficiency and strong task performance. Extensive experiments on arithmetic reasoning, commonsense reasoning, and instruction following tasks demonstrate that AdaMoA consistently outperforms the original MoA across all task categories. Overall, it achieves an average accuracy improvement of 2.38% while substantially reducing token costs by an average of 61.8%, highlighting its strong effectiveness and scalability.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SBA-Route: Domain-Based Routing for Scalable and Low-Latency 5G Distributed Control Planes.
abstract: The transition to distributed 5G/6G architectures reveals a fundamental gap: the Service-Based Architecture (SBA) lacks a scalable routing substrate, directly degrading end-to-end Quality of Service (QoS) for latency-sensitive mobile applications. While the Network Repository Function (NRF) handles service discovery, 3GPP standards provide no routing protocol for information propagation across distributed NRFs. This omission causes inefficient edge-to-edge discovery that inflates handover latency, quadratic configuration complexity, and network-wide routing instability. Since no routing protocol exists for the distributed SBA control plane, existing approaches resort to nonrouting workarounds such as caching or Network Function (NF) replication, which cannot fundamentally resolve these issues. We propose SBA-Route, a domain-based routing framework for the SBA discovery substrate. By organizing NRFs into domains with intra-domain flooding and inter-domain aggregated advertisement, SBA-Route enables direct edge-to-edge discovery and reduces peering complexity from $O\left(N^{2}\right)$ to $O(N)$. Its route aggregation and damping mechanisms further suppress instability. Evaluations demonstrate that SBA-Route reduces inter-domain handover latency by up to 76.6%, lowers central NRF CPU usage by 74%, and suppresses routing oscillations by 71.7%, significantly improving QoS for mobile users in distributed deployments.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Distributed or Centralized: Edge-Cloud Collaborative Active Learning.
abstract: Active Learning (AL) aims to improve model performance by selecting the most informative samples from a pool of unlabeled data under a limited annotation budget. However, most existing active learning methods are designed for centralized settings and cannot be directly applied to edge-cloud collaborative learning systems, which have been widely adopted for edge intelligence. In this work, we propose Edge-Cloud Collaborative Active Learning (ECAL), an efficient two-stage data selection framework. ECAL employs distributed edge nodes to collaboratively pre-filter data using coordination information generated by the cloud, thereby reducing data transmission overhead between edge nodes and the cloud. Furthermore, ECAL offloads part of the data selection workload from the cloud to edge nodes. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that ECAL significantly improves model performance under fixed annotation budgets compared with state-of-the-art non-collaborative baselines.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: TSN-FLARE: A Flexible and Resilient Telemetry Framework for Time-Sensitive Networking.
abstract: As Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) emerges as a critical technology for applications requiring deterministic data transmission, continuous network visibility is essential for sustaining long-term service availability. Real-time telemetry provides this visibility, yet existing frameworks lack the flexibility and resilience demanded by TSN environments. Specifically, semantic coupling binds telemetry metrics to data-plane logic, requiring disruptive recompilation for new metrics, while delivery fragility leads to telemetry loss under strict scheduling constraints and link faults. We present TSN-FLARE, a flexible and resilient telemetry framework for TSN. TSN-FLARE adopts a software-hardware decoupled architecture in which the control plane compiles high-level intents into semantics-oblivious instructions, enabling runtime metric definition without firmware recompilation. For resilient delivery, the framework integrates Slot-Aware Adaptive Routing to accommodate telemetry packets within TSN time-slot constraints and Link-Fault-Aware Feedback to preserve reporting continuity under link faults. Evaluations on an FPGA prototype and large-scale simulations demonstrate that TSN-FLARE achieves millisecond-level metric reconfiguration with less than 3% hardware overhead and deterministic microsecondlevel switch processing latency. Moreover, it maintains resilient delivery even under stringent $5 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ transmission windows and link faults, achieving fewer path hops than baseline approaches.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CBDDoSCLIP: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for Carpet-Bombing DDoS Attack Detection.
abstract: Carpet-bombing DDoS spreads low-rate traffic across many IPs within a /24 subnet, keeping per-host volume within normal ranges and defeating threshold-based detectors. CBDDoSCLIP converts backbone traffic into time–destination-IP CB Images and aligns them with CLIP text for multimodal detection at low trainable-parameter cost. Contributions: (i) CB Images with time binning and IP ordering for simultaneous and sequential patterns; (ii) dual visual encoder, DDoSAdapter residual adaptation, and candidate prompt selection; (iii) training only adapter and projection layers with frozen encoders (~1M parameters). On CICDDoS2019/CICIDS2017 splits and a 100k-sample backbone test set, CBDDoSCLIP matches full fine-tuning accuracy at lower parameter and training cost.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: DMKG: DDoS Defense Enhanced by Multimodal Knowledge Graph Data.
abstract: Modern DDoS attacks increasingly employ multivector combinations, low-rate behaviors, and traffic mimicry to evade detection. Existing deep learning-based defenses efficiently analyze low-level telemetry but usually act as semantic black boxes without explicit mitigation logic. Conversely, Large Language Model (LLM)-based defense systems frequently hallucinate when detached from factual traffic evidence and domain-specific causal constraints. To bridge this gap, we propose DMKG, a multimodal knowledge graph-driven DDoS defense framework that connects low-level traffic evidence with high-level defense knowledge. DMKG constructs a DDoS-specific KG from expert manuals, system alerts, and PCAP-derived evidence, and designs PCAPBERT to anchor PCAP traffic to symbolic attack categories through metric learning. Based on the generated factual traffic summaries, we further develop DDoSRAG to enforce explicit meta-path constraints and reconstruct complete attack-defense causal chains, grounding LLM generation in structured expert logic. Evaluations on a unified benchmark built from CICIDS2017 and CICDDoS2019 demonstrate that DMKG achieves strong performance in Defensive Strategy Recommendation, Context-aware Attack Chain Completion, and Causal Reasoning Explainability. The quantitative results further show that DMKG consistently outperforms pure LLM and standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation baselines.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: HyperWeave: QoS-aware GPU Overcommitment for Deep Learning Training Jobs.
abstract: Low GPU utilization in Deep Learning Training (DLT) clusters severely degrades service quality, manifesting as prolonged Job Completion Time (JCT) and excessive queuing delays. This inefficiency stems from “False Saturation”, where schedulers—misled by rigid capacity constraints and inflated resource profiling—reject incoming jobs despite significant idle physical resources. To minimize JCT and guarantee QoS without expanding hardware, we propose HyperWeave, a QoS-preserving DLT scheduler that enables controlled GPU overcommitment. HyperWeave tackles overcommitment-caused resource contention along temporal and spatial dimensions. (1) Interference-Aware Packing: We propose a Complementary Matching Algorithm (CMA) that identifies and pairs jobs with complementary resource footprints (e.g., interleaving I/O-bound and Computebound stages) to mitigate resource contention in the temporal dimension. (2) Latency-Aware Mapping: We design a Multi-GPU Orchestration Algorithm (MOA) that employs a bucket-based Shortest-Remaining-Service-First (SRSF) strategy to eliminate Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking and mitigate straggler problem in the spatial dimension. Evaluation on a real-world testbed shows that HyperWeave effectively eliminates False Saturation, improving average JCT by $2.93 \times \sim 3.97 \times$ compared to state-ofthe-art schedulers, significantly enhancing cluster service quality.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Chain-Based Service Function Chain Placement: Optimizing Latency in Multi-Topology Networks.
abstract: The widespread adoption of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) enables flexible, cost-effective deployment of network services on commodity servers. In many enterprise scenarios such as security service provisioning, minimizing the end-to-end latency of chain-based service function chains (SFCs) is crucial for improving Quality of Service (QoS). However, the optimal deployment problem is NP-hard, making exact solutions prohibitive at scale. In this paper, we study latency-aware placement of exclusive chain-based SFCs in multi-topology networks under two communication regimes: (i) approximately equal inter-server communication time (typical in intra-datacenter settings) and (ii) unequal communication time on general graphs (common in geo-distributed edge and multi-datacenter settings). We propose a latency-prioritized deployment framework with provable guarantees, including a Swap-and-Sort Based Placement (SSBP) for the equal-time regime and a capacity-aware Spanning-Tree Based Placement (STBP) for the unequal-time regime. We implement the proposed methods on a real testbed spanning eight geographically distributed data centers with real service workloads. Experiments show that our approach reduces endto-end latency by up to 60% over representative spanningtree baselines in heterogeneous networks while maintaining low scheduling overhead. To our knowledge, this is among the first to combine provable guarantees with a real multi-datacenter testbed for latency-aware chain-based SFC placement, providing practical guidance for QoS-aware service deployment.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Asymmetric-Aware Hybrid Granularity Load Balancing in RDMA-enabled Data Center Networks.
abstract: With the widespread deployment of RDMA technology in modern data centers, efficient load balancing is crucial for improving network utilization, reducing flow completion times, and ensuring quality of service (QoS) guarantees. However, existing schemes often fail to perceive network topology asymmetry and frequently cannot accurately identify the locations of asymmetric links, resulting in increased tail latency and degraded throughput. In this paper, we propose A2HG, an asymmetricaware hybrid granularity load balancing in RDMA-enabled datacenter networks. A2HG leverages local port statistics combined with multi-path latency measurements to dynamically detect asymmetric links and assess their impact. Then it adaptively selects the switching granularity according to flow criticality, forwarding critical flows at the packet level and prioritizing them on high-quality paths to minimize reordering, while forwarding non-critical flows at the flow level to fully utilize the available bandwidth of lower-quality paths. Experimental results on both small-scale testbeds and large-scale NS-3 simulations demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art schemes, A2HG can reduce the average flow completion time by up to 64% and the 99th percentile flow completion time by up to 41%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Prediction-Based Adaptive Edge Caching Update Strategy for the Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: The integration of IoV and MEC leads to a surge in delay-sensitive content requests. In viaduct scenarios, 3D structures cause frequent LOS/NLOS transitions, posing challenges to traditional edge caching. This paper presents an edge intelligencebased adaptive caching framework with LSTM popularity prediction and DQN decision-making. Experiments on real-world SUMO trajectories show that our method achieves 77.35% cache hit ratio and 31.2 ms average latency, which outperforms baseline schemes by up to $\mathbf{6. 0 6 \%}$ and $\mathbf{1 1. 4 \%}$, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: QoS, Privacy, and Security Challenges in Deploying Metaverse-Based Virtual Reality Learning for Children with Dyslexia: A Case Study.
abstract: Metaverse-based virtual reality (VR) applications hold significant promise for supporting children with dyslexia through immersive, personalized learning experiences. However, deploying such applications in real-world settings with vulnerable populations introduces operational challenges that the existing literature has not adequately addressed. This paper presents a case study of a metaverse-based VR learning application deployed with 12 children with dyslexia aged 8 to 13 years, primarily in therapy centers in the UAE, examining the quality of service (QoS), privacy, and security challenges encountered. Drawing on direct observations using Meta Quest 3 VR headsets and the Frame platform, we document QoS-related challenges, privacy risks specific to AI-enabled metaverse applications, and security challenges inherent to multi-stakeholder deployments involving vulnerable populations. We further present a cross-dimensional analysis demonstrating that these challenges interact in ways that carry ethical weight: QoS degradation affects learning continuity, privacy gaps expose sensitive disability-related data, and inadequate security puts vulnerable children at risk. Based on these findings, we propose five design guidelines for developers, institutions, and practitioners. This work contributes empirical grounding to an underexplored intersection of QoS, privacy, security, and vulnerable population deployment in educational metaverse contexts.

title: DistSRE: Synthesizing Runtime Executions with Automated Co-Optimization for Distributed LLM Training.
abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) necessitates efficient distributed training across GPU clusters. However, existing distributed training frameworks suffer from isolated performance modeling, high configuration synthesis costs, and restricted operator-level overlap. To address these problems, we propose DistSRE, an automated system that unifies strategy, execution, and resource management into a single cooptimization task. DistSRE is driven by three key designs: (1) a resource-centric performance predictor that accurately models the coupled effects of hardware resources and overlap mechanisms; (2) a hierarchical synthesis algorithm based on counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) that efficiently navigates the NP-hard search space; and (3) a runtime scheduling scheme that tightly coordinates PCIe data movement with GPU computation and NVLink communication. Evaluations GPT-3 models (1.3B-13B) on a 32-GPU NVIDIA A100 cluster training demonstrate that DistSRE reduces end-to-end training time by $\mathbf{1 1. 3 2} \boldsymbol{\%}$ to $\mathbf{2 3. 4 2} \boldsymbol{\%}$ compared to state-of-the-art baselines like Megatron-LM and Aceso.

title: Minimizing the Delay Disparity for Cross-Region Virtual Reality Gaming in Satellite Edge Computing.
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) gaming is one of the delay-sensitive services that require guaranteeing ultra-low and fair delay experience for their users. A conventional VR gaming service is hosted in ground data centers and only admits players from the same geographical region to guarantee a fair experienced delay of players. Cross-region VR gaming in such service deployments leads to large delay disparity among players in different regions, since players in different regions have varying ground network accessibility. In contrast, satellite edge computing (SEC) that integrates satellite communication and edge computing bypasses ground network barriers, making it the only option for cross-region VR gaming. In this paper, we investigate a fundamental problem of multi-player cross-region VR gaming with the aim of guaranteeing a fair gaming experience for players. We first formulate an optimization problem of the delay disparity minimization problem for a multi-player cross-region VR gaming service in an SEC network. We propose an approximation algorithm with an approximation ratio by leveraging a non-trivial transformation into the capacitated K-center problem. We also consider the scenario where the actions of players in VR gaming services are bursty and uncertain, by formulating the online delay disparity minimization problem for multiple cross-region VR gaming services with bursty player actions in an SEC network. We devise an online learning algorithm with a bounded regret by adopting a multi-armed bandit method. We finally evaluate the algorithm performance via extensive simulations based on real satellite network topologies generated by Ansys Systems Tool Kit (STK). Results show that our algorithms outperform their counterparts by achieving $\mathbf{2 5. 6 \%}$ lower the delay disparity.

title: Entangled Photon Source Pooling and Entanglement Distribution for Quantum Networks.
abstract: Entanglement distribution is a key problem in quantum networks. Conventional works on entanglement distribution either ignored that Entangled Photon Sources (EPSes) are precious resources or organized EPSes in an unscalable way. In this work, we propose an EPS Pooling and Entanglement Distribution (EPED) approach to efficiently utilize EPSes. The salient features of EPED include (i) EPSes are organized as several EPS pools; (ii) each EPS pool distributes entanglements only in its coverage area; and (iii) EPSes are dynamically assigned to create different entanglement links. There are two challenges in EPED: (i) when deploying EPS pools, we do not have any demand information; and (ii) we have to calculate the Entanglement Path (EP) for each demand as quickly as possible. To tackle these challenges, we design an algorithm with a constant approximation ratio to minimize the number of EPS pools required, and determine the number of EPSes provisioned to each pool using a primal-dual technique. By preparing candidate EPs for each demand, we solve the online EP selection problem for tens of demands in a network with hundreds of nodes in 6.5 ms. Extensive simulations show that EPED can save up to 8% EPS pools and enhance network throughput by up to 48%.

title: SketchPlan: Full-Visibility Sketch-Based Telemetry with Limited Programmable Switch Coverage.
abstract: Sketch-based in-network telemetry relies on programmable switches for flow visibility. In practice, programmable switches are deployed sparsely, leaving many flows unobservable under passive measurement and causing irreversible visibility loss. Existing systems assume sufficient programmable switch coverage and do not address this limitation. This paper presents SketchPlan, a telemetry framework that restores full flow visibility under partial programmable switch deployment. SketchPlan selectively mirrors traffic from legacy switches to programmable switches for measurement. It reduces mirroring overhead by selecting a minimal set of mirroring points. It enables scalable measurement through sketch-signature-based sharing with lightweight isolation. It further minimizes delivery cost under network and switch resource constraints. We implement a prototype of SketchPlan on Tofino switches. Evaluation results show that SketchPlan can achieve measurement accuracy close to an ideal full-coverage deployment with modest overhead, while scaling efficiently to large datacenter topologies.

title: Semantic Raft: A Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent Inference Framework for Reliable LLM Services.
abstract: The reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in long-horizon tasks remains a critical bottleneck for Modelas-a-Service (MaaS) deployments. Probabilistic semantic failures in LLMs often manifest as Byzantine-like Behaviors (e.g., logic hallucinations), leading to intermediate state pollution and cascading service failures that unstructured multi-agent debates fail to contain. This paper proposes Semantic Raft, a Probabilistic Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Middleware that formalizes multi-agent inference as a Semantic Replicated State Machine. By adapting the Raft consensus protocol with QoS-aware resource scheduling and Prompt-Enforced Blind Verification, our framework constructs logical firewalls to intercept Correlated Failures at the protocol level. Extensive evaluations on high-failure benchmarks demonstrate significant robustness improvements. Notably, Semantic Raft achieves a 37.2% increase in service success rate on long-chain logical reasoning tasks (CLUTRR) compared to standard debate methods. Furthermore, it exhibits ComplexityAdaptive overhead characteristics, providing an economically viable QoS optimization solution for mission-critical AI services.

title: LADS: Towards Low-Latency Atomicity Interval for Cross-shard Transactions via Dynamic Queue Scheduling.
abstract: In sharded blockchains, cross-shard transactions (CTXs) inherently suffer from high confirmation latency. This occurs because each CTX is decomposed into two dependent components-a source and a destination sub-transaction-executed sequentially across different shards. This strict dependency exposes CTXs to unbounded delays and severe unfairness compared to independent intra-shard transactions (ITXs). While ensuring atomicity is mandatory, minimizing the latency interval between these sub-transactions remains a critical open challenge. To address this, we propose LADS (Low-latency Atomicity-Driven Scheduling), a decentralized online scheduling framework. LADS conceptualizes the strict temporal dependency as a quantifiable “Atomicity Debt”. By formulating the transaction scheduling as a stochastic optimization problem, we derive an efficient primaldual algorithm using the Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty technique. This allows each shard to make local, dynamic decisions that balance system throughput against the accumulated debt of pending CTXs. Analysis proves that LADS not only ensures strong queue stability but also establishes a deterministic upper bound on the cross-shard atomicity interval, effectively preventing perpetual starvation. We implement LADS on the opensource BlockEmulator testbed and evaluate it using real-world Ethereum traces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LADS significantly minimizes the average CTX queueing latency and uniquely eliminates systemic discrimination, achieving a solid fairness ratio between ITXs and CTXs even under extreme congestion.

title: Inferring Starlink Latency Structure from Public RIPE Atlas Measurements.
abstract: Most Starlink measurement studies rely on owned dishes, browser extensions, or active scans of the terrestrial network-all of which require infrastructure that an outside reader cannot easily reproduce. We ask the opposite question: how much can be inferred about Starlink latency from public RIPE Atlas built-in pings alone, and where does this approach fall short? Our data combines 897,949 ping samples from 122 RIPE Atlas probes on SpaceX AS14593 (Starlink’s autonomous system) over a 7-day window, the public Starlink TLE catalogue, and a 42-entry corpus of publicly disclosed Starlink-related entities (FCC-licensed earth stations, peering/PoP locations inferred from public BGP, known IXP sites). We find three things. First, perprobe median RTT (round-trip time) groups into four broad latency clusters with centers near 23, 42, 71, and 125 ms. Second, the great-circle distance to the nearest disclosed entity, $d_{\text {pub }}$, is moderately correlated with RTT (Spearman $\rho_{s}=0.40$). The slowest cluster contains both probes that are geometrically far from any disclosed entity (Marshall Is., Guam) and probes whose RTT is not explained by $d_{\text {pub }}$ alone (Mongolia, Iran, Jordan). Third, built-in pings fire around every 240 s. This sampling rate is too sparse to resolve the 15 s satellite handover events reported by owned-dish studies. Two limitations apply throughout: rootDNS targets are anycast, so RTT mixes Starlink’s path with DNS routing; and the public infrastructure corpus is sparse outside North America and Europe.

title: DNSMedic: Automated Precision Diagnosis and Repair Guidance for DNS Misconfigurations.
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) misconfiguration can result in severe social and financial consequences due to its reliance on complex distributed record management. Although some tools can detect and verify DNS configurations, current research still lacks effective formal automated tools for diagnosing and repairing DNS misconfigurations. We propose DNSMedic, a framework that integrates tightly with existing verifiers, to address this issue. Our core insight is to treat the DNS configuration as a program. Based on this insight, it includes two stages: diagnosis and repair. And it mainly has three components: (1) an analyzer that translates traces into Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) formulas and uses Minimum Unsatisfiable Core (MUC) analysis to locate erroneous records automatically; (2) a repair algorithm that progressively expands the repair scope and intelligently defines the value space; (3) two structures that form a storage structure that supports error equivalence class partitioning, supplemented by a graph structure of the global trace graph to analyze the degree of impact. This design achieves a closed-loop “verification-diagnosis-repair” workflow. In the evaluation, DNSMedic accurately repairs the misconfigurations we support; its EEC mechanism significantly reduced the number of repair iterations by 65.9%.

title: MPFV: Lightweight Multipath Forwarding Validation for SRv6 Networks.
abstract: This paper presents MPFV (Multipath Forwarding Validation), a novel path validation mechanism that resolves the fundamental conflict between SRv6’s dynamic multipath forwarding and existing static path verification approaches. By introducing probabilistic authentication with constant computational complexity and dynamic next-hop embedding, MPFV achieves both security and flexibility without compromising performance. Experimental results on the BMv2 platform demonstrate that MPFV improves bandwidth by 13–41% over native SRv6 while adding only 20ms latency in 8-hop scenarios, outperforming PPV by 67.7% and EPIC by 92%. The proposed mechanism effectively defends against path manipulation, packet damage, replay, and verification-induced resource attacks through its three-layer security architecture. MPFV establishes a practical foundation for secure large-scale SRv6 deployment by balancing dynamic path adaptability with end-to-end authenticity.

title: OpScope: Exploiting Operation-Driven Visual Scope for QoS-Stable Cloud Gaming.
abstract: Cloud gaming systems must sustain high visual quality and low interaction latency under dynamic workloads and unstable networks. Existing adaptation mechanisms are often bitrate-centric or limited to video coding optimization, leaving edge-side enhancement weakly connected with the rest of the system. This paper presents OpScope, an operation-driven cloud-edge framework that uses lightweight visual scopes to connect user inputs, motion vectors, residuals, buffering, and edge-side super-resolution. OpScope exploits the locality of user-induced visual changes to distinguish regions that require enhancement from regions that can reuse high-resolution references. Instead of applying full-frame super-resolution to every decoded frame, OpScope recovers non-key frames using motion vectors and residuals, while applying full enhancement only to selected reference frames or regions that cannot be reliably recovered. Experiments on multiple commercial games show that OpScope improves effective pixel throughput by up to 4.71×, reduces end-to-end latency by about $31\%$, and lowers frame drop ratio by $4.9\%$ under network fluctuations, with negligible visual quality loss.

title: Joint Optimization of MEC Offloading and Traffic Signal Control via Diffusion-based Hierarchical DRL.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of vehicular applications has intensified the demand for Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). Existing resource management strategies typically treat Traffic Signal Control (TSC) as a static environmental constraint, ignoring the coupling effect between vehicles’ mobility and computational power. In this paper, we propose Joint Optimization via Diffusion-based Hierarchical DRL (JO-DHD) to synergize active traffic regulation with task offloading. Specifically, we design a hierarchical control mechanism in which the high-level agent manipulates traffic signals to form ad hoc vehicular computing clusters during high-load periods, thereby converting temporary vehicle aggregation into usable computational capacity. To address the resulting high-dimensional hybrid action space, we introduce a conditional diffusion-based actor that uses a conditional diffusion process for policy generation. Extensive experiments show that JO-DHD outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 9.8% in composite performance, achieving an optimal trade-off between mobility efficiency and computational latency.

title: Location-Aware SerDes Configuration for Robust Scale-Up AI Rack Systems.
abstract: Rack-scale AI systems integrate tens of accelerators through tightly coupled scale-up interconnects, where link reliability increasingly depends on physical channel diversity rather than protocol-level design. Accelerator trays located at different rack positions experience heterogeneous signal integrity (SI) conditions due to variations in cable length, loss, reflection, and thermal environment. Conventional approaches rely on protocol-based link training or static firmware configurations, which often fail to deliver robust performance across all rack locations and introduce significant operational complexity. This paper presents a location-aware SerDes configuration framework that exploits stable physical topology information to proactively adopt optimized SerDes parameters per link. By integrating hierarchical rack- and module-level identification with firmware-based parameter selection, the system dynamically applies pre-characterized SerDes settings without modifying existing OAM specifications. Experience from a production Gaudi rack-scale system shows that location-aware configuration can improve bit error rate (BER) by up to three orders of magnitude compared to link training, while simplifying firmware maintenance and tray replacement. This work highlights physical location as a firstclass abstraction for future scale-up infrastructure.

title: RGB: Resource Graph Base for Integrating Tri-Elements in Computing Power Networks.
abstract: Intelligent scheduling is pivotal for unlocking the service potential of Computing Power Networks (CPNs), which requires joint optimization of computing power, algorithms, and data. Analogous to image creation which relies on the blending of primary colors, Quality of Service (QoS) is not dictated by any single element but rather by the synergistic alignment of these three elements. However, existing methods often fail to characterize such collaborative effects, struggling to capture the cross-element dependencies and their impact on scheduling decisions. To address these limitations, we propose RGB-Painter, a Resource Graph-Based scheduling framework that leverages the synergistic interplay among these elements for collaborationaware scheduling in CPNs. Specifically, we construct a trielement resource graph to integrate the three elements and employ graph neural networks to learn fused representations of their dynamic couplings. We then incorporate these embeddings into a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning module equipped with an action masking mechanism, enabling efficient distributed scheduling decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that RGB-Painter reduces the average task completion time by 5.48%-42.58% compared with multiple baselines, validating its efficacy for deployment in real-world CPNs.

title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification.
abstract: Pre-trained models operating directly on raw bytes have achieved promising performance in encrypted network traffic classification (NTC), but often suffer from shortcut learning-relying on spurious correlations that fail to generalize to real-world data. Existing solutions heavily rely on model-specific interpretation techniques, which lack adaptability and generality across different model architectures and deployment scenarios. In this paper, we propose BiasSeeker, the first semi-automated framework that is both model-agnostic and data-driven for detecting dataset-specific shortcut features in encrypted traffic. By performing statistical correlation analysis directly on raw binary traffic, BiasSeeker identifies spurious or environment-entangled features that may compromise generalization, independent of any classifier. To address the diverse nature of shortcut features, we introduce a systematic categorization and apply category-specific validation strategies that reduce bias while preserving meaningful information. We evaluate BiasSeeker on 19 public datasets across three NTC tasks. By emphasizing context-aware feature selection and dataset-specific diagnosis, BiasSeeker offers a novel perspective for understanding and addressing shortcut learning in encrypted network traffic classification, raising awareness that feature selection should be an intentional and scenario-sensitive step prior to model training.

title: SE-STGAE: A Shapelet-Enhanced Spatiotemporal Graph Autoencoder for Early Anomaly Detection.
abstract: Early anomaly detection in networked sensing is crucial for maintaining the Quality of Service (QoS), especially under strict False Positive Rate (FPR) budgets where alarms must be early and reliable. Existing methods typically learn normal spatiotemporal patterns from multi-node sensing streams and raise alarms using reconstruction deviations in a one-class manner. However, in real freeway monitoring, anomalies exhibit complex spatiotemporal propagation and the early anomaly signals are sparse. Meanwhile, traffic streams contain diverse normal fluctuations that may look abnormal, making them hard to distinguish from real incidents. Together, these factors make anomaly propagation hard to capture under strict low-FPR earlywarning settings. To address these challenges, we propose SE-STGAE, a shapelet-enhanced spatiotemporal graph autoencoder. It first uses shapelets to extract localized segment-level precursors, then integrates temporal precursors with propagationaware spatial dependencies to improve robustness to normal fluctuations, and finally applies a tail-emphasized Top-K scoring rule with pure-normal calibration for reliable early alarming. Extensive experiments on real-world freeway datasets show consistent gains over state-of-the-art baselines across datasets and FPR budgets, delivering earlier detection with localized evidence.

title: Purification and Routing for Makespan Minimization in Quantum Networks.
abstract: Collaborative quantum tasks, such as distributed quantum computation, require all entanglement connections to be established before execution can begin. The task completion time is determined by the slowest connection-the makespan. Existing entanglement routing and purification algorithms optimize throughput by selecting a subset of flows to serve, and do not model purification latency, leaving collaborative tasks-where every request must be delivered-without a viable solution. We propose JTPR, which jointly optimizes path selection, purification strategy, and temporal scheduling to minimize makespan while ensuring that every request receives a feasible schedule. JTPR introduces a latency-aware purification model that captures the trade-off between parallel mode (fast but memory-intensive) and serial mode (slow but memory-efficient). A time-indexed integer linear program coordinates all requests over a discretized scheduling horizon, exploiting temporal resource sharing to compact executions. Extensive simulations show that JTPR reduces makespan by 50-62% compared to adapted baselines while scheduling all requests in the tested instances, and ablation analysis reveals how routing diversity, purificationmode flexibility, and temporal scheduling interact under resource contention.

title: UPServe: Backend Agnostic Proxy for Black-box Heterogeneous LLM Scheduling.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is increasingly deployed in heterogeneous environments, demanding efficient serving across diverse hardware platforms and backend engines. While existing load balancers and specialized serving systems facilitate request routing, they still suffer from various limitations, manifested in metric misalignment and observability gaps of black-box backends, non-linear performance degradation under heterogeneity, and conflicting multi-objective optimization goals. To solve these problems, we propose UPServe, a backendagnostic proxy designed for stateless LLM serving, which features three key designs: (1) a phase-aware cost modeling to estimate inference costs without relying on engine internals, (2) a unified score-based scheduling mechanism that integrates phase-aware concurrency and hardware speed normalization to handle heterogeneous non-linear degradation, and (3) an online scheduling algorithm named Phase-Aware Weighted Least Connections (PA-WLC) that drives adaptive dispatching to balance tail latency and aggregate throughput. Finally, we implement UPServe as a transparent proxy and conduct experiments for evaluations in heterogeneous environments. Comparison results demonstrate that UPServe significantly outperforms existing baselines, which reduces tail latency by up to 2.6$\times$ (P99 TTFT) and 2.1$\times$ (P99 TPOT), and improves aggregate throughput by up to 16%. Besides, UPServe operates without modifying inference engine internals, and incurs a negligible scheduling overhead of less than 0.3 ms per request.

title: StarRound: An Efficient Multiple Geographic Region-Avoidance Mechanism for High Dynamic LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellite Networks (LSNs) provide global coverage and low-latency services for long-haul communication. However, unlike existing terrestrial networks, LSNs operate in highly dynamic environments where satellites continuously traverse multiple geographic regions that may experience natural impacts or region-specific interference. Avoiding such regions is challenging due to the high LEO dynamics: fixed geographic regions do not correspond to fixed satellite sets, and the spatial relationships among multiple regions further increase routing complexity. To address this problem, this paper presents StarRound, a geographic region-avoidance mechanism tailored for dynamic LSNs. StarRound introduces the concept of Low-risk Available Planes (LAPs), which transforms dynamic satellite-level region changes into more stable plane-level availability. We implement a prototype of StarRound and conduct large-scale simulations based on real-world LSN information. Evaluation results demonstrate that StarRound can effectively avoid multiple geographic regions and maintain high reachability, while significantly reducing path computation time compared to existing satellite-level pruning approaches.

title: Duet: Towards Efficient and Accurate Sketch-Based Measurement on DPUs.
abstract: Sketch-based measurement has become a fundamental primitive for monitoring network traffic and supporting performance-critical data center applications. However, existing approaches for deploying sketches on DPUs either underutilize DPU hardware capabilities or suffer from degraded accuracy due to limited Arm-side processing capacity and multi-core contention. In particular, most designs directly port host-side sketch implementations to the DPU Arm subsystem, introducing excessive forwarding overhead and hardware pressure. In this paper, we present Duet, an efficient and accurate sketch-based measurement on DPUs. Duet adopts a layered measurement architecture that dynamically schedules flows between Arm-based sketches and the DPU hardware forwarding pipeline according to traffic characteristics. Heavy flows are offloaded to hardware tables to leverage line-rate processing and relieve Arm-side contention, while light flows are retained in software sketches to avoid excessive hardware table updates. To further address crosslayer aggregation and multi-core concurrency challenges, Duet incorporates a zeroing mechanism and lock-free optimizations to ensure measurement consistency and accuracy. We implement Duet on an NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPU and conduct extensive experiments on a real testbed. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with traditional sketch-based measurement approaches, Duet improves throughput by a factor of approximately $7.1 \times$, packet rate by a factor of approximately $28.9 \times$, and measurement accuracy by approximately 50.1%.

title: Ensuring QoS Stability in Dynamic WANs through Selectively Optimized Range Routing.
abstract: Network traffic volatility frequently causes severe Quality of Service (QoS) degradation. Preventing this degradation requires Traffic Engineering (TE) solutions that maintain robustness against dynamic traffic shifts, preserve scalability for computational efficiency, and operate effectively with limited historical data. However, existing TE solutions fail to satisfy these three conditions simultaneously. Conventional mathematical model-based solutions struggle to balance between scalability and resilience to traffic variations. While recent deep learningbased solutions demonstrate strong scalability and robustness, their performance depends heavily on massive datasets of Traffic Matrices (TMs). To resolve these limitations and guarantee QoS, we propose Selectively Optimized Range Routing (SORR) to satisfy all three TE requirements through two core schemes. First, SORR reduces the dependence on massive historical TMs by employing a data-model hybrid architecture that synergistically combines deep reinforcement learning with established mathematical routing models. Second, it leverages a hierarchical collaborative optimization strategy that distributes TE tasks across different routing models according to their specific operational roles, ensuring both high scalability and resilience. Evaluations using public datasets and real traffic traces confirm that SORR delivers good performance using as few as 96 TMs. Compared to existing solutions, SORR improves the worst-case performance by 79% while conceding only a 2% reduction in median-case performance.

title: ClusterFi: Enabling Concurrent WiFi Backscatter Communication via Collided Signal Clustering.
abstract: Owing to the widespread deployment of WiFi infrastructures, the ubiquitous availability of WiFi signals, and the inherent tolerance to signal collisions, concurrent WiFi backscatter communication has attracted significant attention in recent years. However, existing concurrent WiFi backscatter designs suffer from fundamental limitations, including unreliable demodulation, limited support for dynamic tag variation, and complex dual-receiver deployments. To overcome these limitations, we propose ClusterFi, a novel concurrent WiFi backscatter system with three key features: robust demodulation even under unreliable WiFi transceiver links, support for IoT scenarios with dynamic tag variation, and effective operation using only a single receiver. These capabilities are enabled by a set of carefully designed techniques, e.g., reference-symbol modulation, an all-ones reference sequence, and a search-based cluster identification method. We evaluate the performance of ClusterFi across a wide range of scenarios. Our results demonstrate that ClusterFi i) achieves a BER on the order of $10^{-5}$ under moderate-quality WiFi transceiver links, which is around $8152 \times$ lower than that of dual-receiver systems; and ii) under dynamic tag variation, ClusterFi obtains a BER of about 0.0005, achieving an approximately 304-fold improvement over its counterpart.

title: CF-BAD: Coarse-to-Fine Granularity BGP Anomaly Detection for Prefix Hijacking.
abstract: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) serves as the defacto standard for inter-domain routing, yet it fundamentally lacks authentication and validation mechanisms, leaving the global Internet infrastructure vulnerable to both malicious attacks and inadvertent misconfigurations. Traditional detection approaches often fall short in accurately identifying prefix hijacking, particularly in small-scale events, and typically produce results that are difficult to interpret. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CF-BAD, a novel anomaly detection framework. Specifically, to capture the subtle patterns characteristic of small-scale anomalies, we construct a dual-granular feature tensor that integrates both time- and frequency-domain information derived from raw BGP data. We further introduce an adaptive mask mechanism tailored for the Swin-Transformer architecture, enabling enhanced representation learning across both coarse- and fine-grained knowledge. Our detection model also incorporates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) unit to effectively capture long- and short-term temporal dependencies. To improve interpretability, we devise a novel layer-wise root cause analysis (RCA) method that provides explainable insights via hierarchical decomposition. Extensive experiments conducted on 15 real-world anomaly events comprising 343 million BGP messages in total demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in both detection and RCA accuracy across the majority of cases.
