title: Efficient and High-Precision Online Backdoor Detection for Unknown Attack Domains.
abstract: Transformer-based language models are increasingly shared and widely employed for various tasks due to their extraordinary capabilities. However, the public models deployed in machine learning as a service system face an increasingly severe threat from backdoor attacks. Existing methods can solve attack domain-specific backdoor attacks that predict poisoned samples to a particular target class, but are inadequate for content generation tasks whose attack domain is unknown. Therefore, we propose a novel and effective online backdoor attack detection method, which works well under unknown attack domains in natural language processing (NLP). The main idea is to explore the differences in attack-related feature maps between inputs with triggers and clean inputs. We have designed and trained a plug-and-play online discriminator module to identify potential inputs with triggers, effectively mitigating the risk of backdoors. Our discriminator module is lightweight, processing 1000 inputs within 1 second. We evaluated our method on both Transformer-based encoder and decoder models, assessing its effectiveness from multiple aspects, including performance against adaptive attacks. The detection performance is improved by 22.58% compared with existing methods and can achieve up to 90% detection accuracy when facing previously unseen triggers. Additionally, our method remains high fidelity, the false positive rate is as low as 7.97% for clean models.

title: ALPS: ACK-induced Latency-based Packet Spraying for Multipath Transmission.
abstract: Multipath transport is essential to achieve high throughput and reliability in data center networks. As the finest-grained load balancing paradigm, adaptive packet spraying faces four well-defined challenges: 1) Self-delayed Feedback: Congestion delays its own feedback, yielding stale spraying weights; 2) Path Weighting Dilemma: Aggressive adaptation induces herd behavior, whereas conservative weighting degrades to random spraying; 3) State Heterogeneity: Inconsistent states across sprayed paths complicate congestion control decisions; 4) Loss-reordering Ambiguity: Spraying-induced reordering obscures genuine loss detection. ALPS addresses these challenges through four mechanisms: 1) ACK-induced Latency Measurement: Reconstruct precise path latency via high-priority ACK on the reverse path to reduce feedback delay; 2) Latency-based Dynamic Weighting: Map latency to weight via a non-linear decay function to favor lowerlatency paths and prevent herd behavior; 3) Collective Congestion Control: Evaluate paths collectively and reduce the rate only when no viable offload path exists, complying with the schedulingfirst principle; 4) Path-aligned Loss Detection: Identify non-tail losses via per-path in-flight tracking and reverse-path ACK fidelity, and distinguish tail loss, link failure, and delayed feedback upon timeout via ghost packets to eliminate false retransmissions. We implement ALPS on FPGA-based SmartNICs with minimal hardware overhead. Large-scale simulations demonstrate that ALPS reduces latency measurement error and feedback delay by 91.69% and 89.23%, respectively. It improves average and P99 FCT by 44.5% and 26.1% over state-of-the-art schemes, and maintains >98% bandwidth utilization 94% of the time.

title: NimbleChain: Automatic Timeout Tuning for PBFT-based Blockchain Systems.
abstract: For the widely deployed PBFT-based blockchain systems, the timeout threshold is crucial in delivering high performance and resilience. However, network dynamics and Byzantine attacks make it difficult to maintain persistent high performance using the static timeout setting. To address the operational challenge, this paper presents the design and implementation of an automatic run-time optimization scheme, NimbleChain, which utilizes a lightweight reinforcement learning technique to dynamically adjust the timeout threshold at each node in a distributed manner. Specifically, it integrates reinforcement learning techniques with the well-known Jacobson algorithm to adapt to network dynamics, and incorporates a failure detection mechanism to adapt to Byzantine attacks. We integrate NimbleChain with Tenderminta production-grade blockchain framework and execute comprehensive benchmarking across heterogeneous environments: containerized local testbeds and geographically distributed Alibaba Cloud clusters. The results demonstrate that NimbleChain enhances throughput by up to 35%, owing to its network dynamics adaptation, and reduces performance degradation by up to 40%, thanks to its Byzantine attacks adaptation.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RAN Parameters Under the Microscope: A Deep Dive into 5G Handover Performance in Dense Urban Network.
abstract: With the development of 5G, various applications are being supported, leading to an increasing requirement for mobility management. Due to the characteristics of millimeter waves and small cell deployment, the performance degradation caused by frequent handover failures (HOF) in dense urban environments is serious. Although Conditional handover (CHO) has been proposed to reduce the high incidence of HOF, the complexity of parameters decided on the Radio Access Network (RAN) leads to some performance bottlenecks. A systematic evaluation of CHO performance from a procedural perspective remains unprecedented. To explore performance issues and their root causes, we modeled the CHO procedure and analyzed the impact of the parameters. An evaluation system has been constructed to assess CHO performance, including a controllable testbed and a group of evaluation benchmarks. We analyzed CHO procedure from parameters of triggering preparation and execution phases, and the impact of user speeds. Several issues have been detected, including misjudgments and PingPong effects, etc. Furthermore, we evaluated performance at the application level, providing guidance on parameter configurations for different applications. The 5G platform has been open-sourced1.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Zephyr: Switch-Aided Weighted Congestion Control for Differentiated Inference Workloads.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is moving toward distributed and disaggregated serving architectures, generating heterogeneous datacenter traffic with diverse quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. However, commodity switches provide only a limited number of hardware priority groups, forcing performance-critical collective communication, prefilldecode (PD) KV cache transfers, and background traffic to share the same physical FIFO queue. Under this constraint, endpoint weighted congestion control offers a practical mechanism for differentiated bandwidth allocation, but endpoint-only recovery lacks direct visibility into bottleneck queue state and can converge slowly under bursty inference traffic.This paper presents Zephyr, a switch-aided weighted congestion control mechanism for differentiated inference transport. Zephyr uses endpoint weighted congestion control to provide fine-grained bandwidth differentiation among traffic classes sharing one physical queue. To accelerate recovery beyond endpointonly control, Zephyr leverages lightweight switch-side queue-state hints to guide sender-side rate adjustment. These hints are reflected by receivers through ACK feedback, enabling senders to modulate the additive-increase step of their AIMD controllers without replacing the underlying transport state machine. NS-3 simulations on a 400 Gbps fat-tree topology show that Zephyr reduces the average and P99 flow completion time (FCT) of all-to-all traffic by 45.21% and 12.22%, respectively. Across mixed workloads, Zephyr reduces overall P99 FCT by 61.76% while keeping latency-sensitive PD KV traffic nearly unaffected.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CoPT: Collaborative Machine-Learning-Based Mechanism for Adaptive Congestion Control Parameter Tuning in Data Center Networks.
abstract: As the types and scale of applications supported by data center networks continue to expand, network traffic characteristics are becoming increasingly complex, exhibiting high dynamism and heterogeneity in both time and space dimensions. Efficient congestion control technology is crucial to optimizing network performance. Adaptive adjustment mechanisms for congestion control parameters based on distributed switches and centralized controllers often exhibit limitations when handling complex and changing traffic characteristics, resulting in poor network performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CoPT, a Collaborative machine-learningbased mechanism for adaptive congestion control Parameter Tuning in data center networks. This mechanism uses a network performance model in the centralized controller to predict portlevel ECN parameters for global network traffic and sends the predictions as “guidance” to the switch control plane. A guided-reinforcement-learning-based agent is deployed on the distributed switch ports. This agent, combined with local traffic characteristics and global ECN parameters, “guides” the selection of optimal parameters, effectively adapting to various complex traffic characteristics and significantly improving network performance. Experimental results show that, under various traffic scenarios, CoPT significantly outperforms both distributed-based and centralized-based methods in terms of flow completion time (FCT) and reduction of average queue length.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Dual-Sketch: A Route-Oblivious Framework for Distributed Sparse Superspreader Detection.
abstract: Detecting sparse superspreaders—hosts with high fan-out but minimal traffic per destination—is vital for exposing stealthy threats like low-rate scanning. However, accurately identifying these sources in distributed network environments remains challenging due to visibility fragmentation across multiple monitors and traffic volume inflation caused by multi-hop routing. This paper proposes Dual-Sketch, a distributed, merge-friendly sketch framework specifically designed for sparse superspreader detection. Dual-Sketch introduces a dual-pool architecture that separately estimates spread and route-oblivious volume using max-mergeable registers, effectively eliminating overcounting errors in complex multi-hop topologies. To ensure high performance and accuracy, Dual-Sketch employs a candidate-gated mechanism driven by register state-change events, which filters background noise and provides unbiased incremental estimation. Experimental results on real-world traces demonstrate that Dual-Sketch achieves an F1 score of up to 97.3% and a processing throughput of 14.12 Mpps, outperforming state-of-the-art solutions by $\mathbf{2. 7 \% - 2 0. 4 \%}$ in detection accuracy while maintaining a compact memory footprint.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CT-Sketch: Persistent Item Lookup Based on Collision Statistics and Thresholds.
abstract: Detecting persistent items that recur across multiple time windows is critical for anomaly monitoring in high-speed data streams, yet it remains challenging under strict memory constraints. Existing methods often suffer from hash collisions and many record redundant information in sketch structures, which exacerbates collisions and degrades both accuracy and throughput. This paper introduces CT-Sketch, an approximate data structure designed for persistence detection. Instead of tracking per-item statistics, our approach maintains a global stream state—including the current window identifier and collision information. We use current window number to set dynamic threshold to protect promising persistent item, while collision information guides the eviction of non-persistent items via dynamically adjusted replacement probabilities. We provide a formal error-bound analysis that establishes the theoretical soundness of CT-Sketch. Evaluations on multiple real-world stream datasets show that CT-Sketch outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives in accuracy and throughput for persistence item lookup and persistence estimation. For example, compared to the stable score, the F1-Score improved $18.13 \%$. ARE reduced 35.11% and improved 51.72% throughput.

title: Beyond Random Probing: Intelligent IPv6 Discovery via Ensemble Learning and Contextual Expansion.
abstract: The vast IPv6 address space renders exhaustive scanning computationally infeasible. We present DeepScan6, a hybrid discovery framework integrating three components: ensemble-based seed preprocessing, a novel Context Expansion (CEX) mechanism, and a tolerance-based incremental learning module. CEX performs prefix-by-prefix IID sequence analysis within individual /64 prefixes and generates candidates through prioritized interpolation and extrapolation. The incremental learning module selectively incorporates newly discovered addresses via lightweight iterative updates, enabling self-improvement across rounds without full retraining. DeepScan6 achieves a 75-77% hit rate on heterogeneous seed sets, outperforming nine baseline methods by 22.1-72.1%. Deployed at scale, it yields 10,139,214 new active addresses beyond the IPv6Hitlist across 1,232 ASes in 92 countries. Measurement reveals severe address concentration (top-3 ASes: 49.89%), extreme subnet sparsity (86.8% of /64 subnets contain one address), 20.87% high-risk IID patterns, and 42.01% of HTTPS-responsive addresses simultaneously exposing HTTP.

title: CEINR: Critical Element-aware In-Network Recovery for Distributed Machine Learning.
abstract: Distributed Machine Learning (DML) accelerates training by sharing workloads across multiple workers, but it is vulnerable to worker failures during training. Existing recovery solutions typically restore failed workers from local checkpoints or remote hosts. When local recovery states are unavailable, however, fetching model parameters from remote hosts incurs high recovery latency and heavy network overhead because large amounts of data must travel over long paths. To address this issue, we propose Critical Element-aware In-Network Recovery (CEINR), a programmable-switch-assisted recovery solution for DML. CEINR moves recovery states from remote hosts into the network by maintaining them during normal training and enabling failed workers to retrieve recovery parameters directly from nearby Top-of-Rack switches. To fit limited switch memory, CEINR further introduces a critical element identification mechanism that keeps only essential model parameters updatable while leaving non-critical parameters fixed. Evaluations on AlexNet and ResNet-18 show that CEINR cuts recovery time by up to 93.15% and recovery traffic by up to 96.00% while preserving high model accuracy.

title: Zero-Cost Merging Transitioning for Large-Scale Erasure-Coded Storage Systems.
abstract: Erasure coding is a storage-efficient fault-tolerance mechanism widely used in large-scale storage systems. To address the high storage cost driven by rapidly growing data volumes, modern erasure-coded systems can employ merging transitioning to further reduce redundancy overhead. However, merging transitioning can incur significant bandwidth costs, potentially degrading system efficiency and quality of service (QoS). Existing merging algorithms aim to mitigate these costs, but we observe that they may still incur excessive overhead due to fluctuating transitioning costs, uncontrollable implicit costs, and complex optimal algorithms. In this paper, we derive conditions on stripe layouts that enable zero transitioning cost and zero implicit costs. Based on these conditions, we propose a stripe placement scheme that can construct three zero-cost layouts. They ensure zero transitioning cost while eliminating different types of implicit costs. We also design a low-complexity optimal algorithm tailored to the proposed layouts. We implement prototypes of the proposed layouts and their dedicated algorithm, and evaluate them through simulations on a single machine and experiments on an Amazon EC2 cluster. The results show that the proposed layouts with the dedicated algorithm achieve the expected zero cost and reduce total execution time by up to 89.3% compared with conventional layouts using existing algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: FedRIDA: Coordinated Participation and Update Control for Time-Efficient Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables distributed clients to collaboratively train a shared model without transferring raw data; however, its practical efficiency is fundamentally constrained by heterogeneous environments. System variability reduces effective participation through stragglers and synchronization delays, while statistical heterogeneity leads to directionally inconsistent updates that slow convergence. These two factors are inherently coupled and jointly determine time-to-accuracy in real-world deployments. To address this latency-consistency tradeoff, FedRIDA coordinates client participation and update influence within a unified framework. It integrates delay-aware scheduling with divergence-aware learning rate adaptation, selecting clients based on both responsiveness and contribution while attenuating the impact of strongly misaligned updates under non-IID data. By jointly regulating participation mass and effective step sizes, FedRIDA directly reduces aggregation variance induced by partial participation and bias caused by gradient inconsistency. We establish convergence under standard smoothness and bounded variance assumptions. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Shakespeare demonstrate consistent improvements in both final accuracy and time-to-accuracy, achieving up to $1.64 \times$ faster convergence and $\mathbf{3. 5 4} \boldsymbol{\%}$ higher test accuracy compared with strong baselines.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: FedCod: An Efficient Coded Communication Protocol for Cross-Silo Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is an innovative distributed machine learning paradigm that enables multiple parties to collaboratively train a model while preserving data privacy. Communication efficiency concerns arise in cross-silo FL, particularly due to the network heterogeneity and fluctuations associated with geo-distributed data silos. Most of the existing solutions to these problems focus on algorithmic improvements that alter the FL algorithm but sacrifice the training performance. How to address these problems from a network perspective that is decoupled from the FL algorithm remains an open challenge. This paper proposes FedCod, the first application-layer coded communication protocol designed for cross-silo FL. FedCod transparently utilizes a coding mechanism to enhance the efficient use of idle bandwidth through client-to-client communication, and dynamically adjusts coding redundancy to mitigate network bottlenecks and fluctuations, thereby improving the communication efficiency and accelerating the FL training process. In our real-world experiments, FedCod demonstrates a significant reduction in average communication time by up to 62% compared to the baseline, while maintaining FL training performance and optimizing inter-client communication traffic.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: GCA-BULF: A Bottom-Up Framework for Short-Term Load Forecasting Using Grouped Critical Appliances.
abstract: With the rise of time-of-use and tiered electricity pricing, energy consumers are encouraged to adopt peak-shifting strategies by automatically controlling high-power appliances. These help lower energy costs while enhancing the power grid's stability. To support such energy management with high resilience and responsiveness, reliable short-term load forecasting (STLF) plays a critical role. STLF predicts electricity consumption over time horizons ranging from minutes to days, using historical data, temporal patterns, and contextual factors. Traditional top-down forecasting methods struggle to capture the complex consumption patterns of diverse and mixed appliance loads. Although bottom-up methods improve forecasting accuracy by integrating appliance-level data, monitoring all appliances is costly, and many do not meaningfully impact total load prediction. Therefore, we propose GCA-BULF, a bottom-up short-term load forecasting framework based on grouped critical appliances, supported by three key designs. First, the Critical Appliance Filtering module ranks appliances according to their power consumption, switching frequency, and usage pattern periodicity, and identifies critical ones through iterative load decomposition. Next, the Related Appliance Grouping module clusters these appliances based on spatial and temporal correlations for group-level forecasting. Finally, the Collaborative Load Forecasting module refines the total load prediction by combining multiple group-level forecasts. We evaluate GCA-BULF on residential and office building load forecasting tasks. Experimental results reveal that GCA-BULF improves hourly total load forecasting by 20.85%-57.88% compared to existing top-down methods and by 33.03%-92.48% compared to bottom-up methods.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: The Imitation Game: Using Large Language Models to Disrupt Chinese Chat-Based Cybercrime.
abstract: Chat-based cybercrime has emerged as a pervasive threat, with attackers leveraging real-time messaging platforms to conduct scams that rely on trust-building, deception, and psychological manipulation. Traditional defense mechanisms, which operate on static rules or shallow content filters, struggle to identify these conversational threats, especially when attackers use multimedia obfuscation and context-aware dialogue. In this work, we ask a provocative question inspired by the classic Imitation Game: Can machines convincingly pose as human victims to turn deception against cybercriminals? We present LURE (LLM-based User Response Engagement), the first system to deploy Large Language Models (LLMs) as active agents (not as passive classifiers) embedded within adversarial chat environments. LURE combines automated discovery, adversarial interaction, and OCR-based analysis of image-embedded payment data. Applied to the setting of Chinese illicit video chat scams on Telegram, our system engaged 53 actors across 98 groups. In over 56% of interactions, the LLM maintained multi-round conversations without being noticed as a bot, effectively “winning” the imitation game. Our findings reveal key behavioral patterns in scam operations, such as payment flows, upselling strategies, and platform migration tactics.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: An Adaptive Multi-Metric Forwarding Strategy for Vehicular Named Data Networking with Hybrid Contention and Opportunistic Delivery.
abstract: Vehicular Named Data Networking (VNDN) requires robust Quality of Service (QoS) for intelligent transportation. However, broadcast storms and network partitions often hinder performance. This paper proposes an Adaptive Multi-Metric Contention and Opportunistic Forwarding (AMCOF) strategy. It uses a lightweight Q-learning agent to tune metric weights based on local density dynamically. The strategy integrates Top-K truncation and a Store-Carry-Forward (SCF) mechanism to handle diverse environments. Simulation results show that AMCOF improves delivery reliability and network efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: LAMP5G: A Link-Aware Multipath QUIC Scheduler for Heterogeneous and Disruption-Prone 5G Cellular Networks.
abstract: Multipath transport has emerged as a promising solution to address key challenges in 5G cellular networks, including improved performance with limited RAN resources, resilience against link failures, and operator heterogeneity. While emerging 5G architectures such as NR dual connectivity (NR-DC) and multi-operator deployments potentially enable simultaneous access to multiple paths, efficiently utilizing these paths remains challenging due to dynamic link conditions, frequent handovers, and environmental impairments.In this paper, we present LAMP5G, a link-aware scheduler built on Multipath QUIC (MPQUIC) for 5G cellular networks. LAMP5G employs a dynamic path-ranking mechanism designed for heterogeneous path environments. The ranking algorithm leverages both end-to-end transport-layer metrics-such as throughput, round-trip time (RTT), loss rate, and congestion window size-and local link-layer statistics to estimate available path bandwidth. To mitigate disruptions caused by handovers, LAMP5G implements a make-before-break strategy through explicit path management, enabling seamless traffic migration between RANs.We evaluate LAMP5G on a 5G testbed. Experimental results show that LAMP5G reduces completion time by 57% compared to the dual-QUIC baseline under heterogeneous path conditions. Furthermore, during mobility scenarios, LAMP5G attains approximately 60% higher average throughput compared to traditional handover.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SOPSmith: Forging Executable SOPs for LLM-Driven GPU Cluster Network Diagnosis.
abstract: GenAI training and inference on GPU clusters place unprecedented demands on the underlying network fabric, where microsecond jitter or a single misbehaving link can cascade into substantial training stalls and SLO violations. The same end-user symptom can originate from RDMA NICs, congestion-control state, switch buffers, or topology asymmetries, with evidence scattered across heterogeneous telemetry. LLM-based agents promise to automate this troubleshooting via open-ended reasoning, but their unstructured exploration is hard to reproduce, audit, and trust. We argue the dominant gap is not language-reasoning capacity but action discipline: what to verify, in what sequence, when to stop, and when to defer to humans. We propose SOPSmith, a paradigm that forges operators’ standard operating procedures into executable control policies governing LLM-agent decision-making for GPU cluster networks; a small empirical probe across seven off-the-shelf LLMs quantifies the tool-call unreliability that motivates this framing. Our goal is not to evaluate a built system but to articulate the problem framing, sketch the design space, and surface open research questions for SOP-grounded diagnosis of GPU cluster networks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: LVProv: A Lightweight Blockchain-Anchored Verifiable Provenance Scheme for High-Dimensional Data.
abstract: Data provenance is crucial for ensuring data trustworthiness, as it traces the entire transfer and evolution of data throughout its lifetime. Meanwhile, with the explosive growth of data, provenance is shifting toward managing multidimensional feature vectors and requires content-based similarity for lineage establishment. This reliance requires approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) on outsourced cloud servers. However, this introduces security risks, as remote infrastructure may tamper with records or ranking results. Unlike blockchain-based schemes that perform complete verification on-chain, blockchain-anchored alternatives have been proposed to ensure provenance security with minimal on-chain overhead. However, existing blockchainanchored verifiable schemes suffer from key limitations that lack support for full-lifetime updates and cannot audit the underlying similarity computation. Moreover, their verification costs increase linearly with data scale. To address these issues, we propose LVProv, a lightweight blockchain-anchored verifiable provenance scheme that first achieves sublinear authentication costs, supports full-lifetime updates, and enables efficient on-chain verification of similarity computations. LVProv introduces three core components. First, it uses a global HNSW-Router for centroid-guided semantic grouping, which reduces the maintenance cost of authenticated data structures from $O(N)$ to $O(\log K)$. Second, it applies Residual Quantization (RQ) to convert compression codes into cryptographic commitments. These commitments allow users to audit server-returned rankings through efficient on-chain verification. Third, it employs lightweight bucket-level Merkle trees with a triple-verification procedure. This procedure ensures routing correctness, data integrity, and computational correctness. LVProv thereby supports efficient full-lifetime data updates. Experimental results demonstrate that LVProv reduces VO size by 69% and achieves 3.4x faster verification than the state of the art, while maintaining high recall.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Breaking the Accuracy-Latency Trade-Off in Sketch Compression for Network Measurement.
abstract: Sketch-based measurement is fundamental for real-time network monitoring, but performing efficient, high-fidelity compression for distributed sketch aggregation remains a critical bottleneck. Current methods present a severe trade-off: grouping-based techniques (e.g., Elastic, Hokusai) are fast but incur unbounded errors, while clustering-based approaches improve accuracy at the cost of prohibitive latency, making neither suitable for real-time control loops. This paper introduces LightRanger (LR), a lightweight compression mechanism designed to break the above trade-off. LightRanger is built on two key designs: (1) real-time value-range grouping, which dynamically sets grouping intervals using observed global extrema to enable low-distortion, uniform bucket mapping; and (2) adaptive bitmap pruning, which strategically reduces transmission overhead under strict bandwidth limits while preserving essential statistical structure. Evaluated across real-world traces (i.e., CAIDA, MAWI, Zipf, and Webdocs) and standard sketches including Count-Min (CM) Sketch, Count-Mean-Min (CMM) Sketch, Conversation-Update (CU) Sketch, and CSM Sketch, LightRanger reduces average relative error by up to $8.92 \times$ over Elastic and $38.59 \times$ over Hokusai, while running $37.23 \times$ faster than clustering-based methods. By decoupling accuracy from latency, LR makes high-fidelity, real-time sketch aggregation practical for bandwidth-constrained distributed monitoring.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: MiniQ: Minimizing Tail Latency for Cloud SFCs with Queuing-aware Execution Planning.
abstract: Service Function Chains (SFCs) increasingly rely on flexible orchestrations to support elastic and latency-sensitive Cloud services. However, existing schemes fail to jointly consider service orders, execution models, and replication strategies due to the complexity of each individual mechanism and the interplay amongst. These factors can induce different packet queue pressure, packet handoff overhead, state synchronization, and resource contention, leading to diverged 95th-percentile (P95) tail latency. Hence, we propose a dependency-informed queuing-aware execution planning framework for Cloud SFCs. The framework models an execution plan over service order, execution model, and replication strategy, and represents execution-induced queue pressure using the Queue Pressure Vector (QPV). Specifically, it translates service dependencies (i.e., data, control, state, and resource dependencies) into queue pressure signals, and uses QPV together with the share of queuing in the overall latency to select execution plans that reduce queuing waiting and tail-latencies. Evaluation results show that the proposed planner reduces P95 latency by approximately $86.4\%$ compared with original pipeline execution while achieving comparable performance to the optimal.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CoInfer: Breaking the Resource Wall for Collaborative Edge Inference.
abstract: Deploying large DNNs on edge devices is severely hindered by strict hardware constraints. Multi-device collaborative inference mitigates this bottleneck. However, existing frameworks struggle in heterogeneous edge environments. They rely on inaccurate theoretical metrics and ignore memory bottlenecks, causing out-of-memory failures. Furthermore, they isolate model partitioning from hardware configurations like dynamic frequency scaling. This isolation yields suboptimal latency and energy trade-offs. To address these challenges, we propose CoInfer, a collaborative edge inference framework, which jointly optimizes model partitioning, device allocation, and frequency scaling. To model hardware heterogeneity, CoInfer introduces a lightweight predictor. This predictor fuses neural network attributes with microarchitectural features to accurately estimate inference latency. Guided by these profiles, a two-level scheduler orchestrates task execution. The upper tier explores the global frequency space. Concurrently, the lower tier executes a memory-constrained hierarchical graph search to identify optimal routing paths. For fault tolerance, CoInfer integrates an adaptive backtracking mechanism to rapidly recover from unexpected node failures. Experiments on a 20 -node cluster show CoInfer reduces scheduling overhead by 42%, and saves up to 46.4% of inference time when device fails unexpectedly. Code is available at the GitHub repository.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: StarkServe: A Framework for Elastic Serverless LLM Inference at the Extreme Edge.
abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) at the extreme edge is hindered by severe resource constraints. While serverless computing offers scale-to-zero efficiency, existing request-level frameworks cannot accommodate the stateful, compute-intensive nature of LLMs. Achieving true elasticity requires Token-Level Statelessness, currently bottlenecked by static model redundancy, rigid GPU allocation, and high statemigration I/O overhead. We propose StarkServe, a serverless inference system that co-designs hardware-aware algorithms with system-level scheduling. StarkServe employs an adaptive skipping mechanism to dynamically prune redundant sublayers at runtime, a multi-tenant GPU runtime enabling fine-grained spatial multiplexing, and an elastic state dispatcher that orchestrates anticipatory KV cache movement to overlap I/O with computation. Experimental results demonstrate that StarkServe significantly reduces end-to-end latency and memory footprint compared to state-of-the-art serverless baselines while preserving generation quality.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Chronus: Accurate and Memory-Efficient Sketching for High-Cumulative-RTT Flow Detection.
abstract: High-Cumulative-RTT flow detection (HCRD) is essential for fine-grained network management and security, as it identifies flows that consistently incur high round-trip times (RTTs), a key indicator of sustained attacks or persistent network congestion. Existing approaches either cannot provide lightweight detection or rely on assumptions that do not reflect practical RTT characteristics. In this paper, we present Chronus, a novel sketch-based framework that tackles these challenges by exploiting the highly skewed nature of RTT distributions at both packet and flow levels. Our key observation is that the vast majority of RTT samples and flows exhibit normal latency, whereas only a small fraction of flows accumulate persistently high RTTs. Guided by this insight, Chronus integrates abnormal RTT filtering, invalid record reclamation, and RTT-aware tracking, enabling reliable RTT sample construction, efficient memory reuse, and preferential retention of high-cumulative-RTT flows under extreme memory budgets (e.g., 64KB). We provide theoretical analysis and implement Chronus on CPU and P4. Experiments on real traffic traces show that Chronus improves F1-score by up to 0.778$\times$ and reduces measurement error by up to 96.636% over state-of-the-art solutions.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: O3-Sketch: Memory-Efficient Online Chaotic Flow Detection in High-Speed Networks.
abstract: Finding chaotic flows with high out-of-order packets is critical for diagnosing performance issues in modern networks. Existing methods either fail to capture packet arrival order or can only handle short-term packet reordering, limiting their accuracy and generality in chaotic flow detection. To address these challenges, we propose O3-sketch, a novel algorithm that exploits the intrinsic out-of-order behavior of network flows. Our key insight is that chaotic flows exhibit stable and persistent reordering over time, while most flows either carry a few outof-order packets or experience transient disorder. O3-sketch incorporates two novel metrics: out-of-order count and in-order gap count into its update strategy. This allows it to efficiently evict normal and transient disordering flows while retaining true chaotic flows with high accuracy, even under extreme memory constraints (e.g., 32KB). We provide rigorous theoretical guarantees for the O3-sketch and implement it on both CPU and P4 platforms. Extensive experiments on real-world traffic traces show that O3-sketch improves F1 score by up to 2.487×, reduces measurement error by at least 90%, and improves processing speed by up to $26.167 \times$ compared to the state-of-the-art.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: DelAct: A Replayable Boundary Runtime for Auditable and Governed LLM Agent Workflows.
abstract: LLM-driven agent workflows increasingly invoke tools that trigger side effects in external systems. When these workflows encounter timeouts or crash mid-execution, the outcome can become uncertain. Naive retries may duplicate actions, while partial effects can leave residual state that complicates incident diagnosis and repair. We observe that current agent stacks lack an explicit, replayable boundary between LLM reasoning and tool execution. This makes postmortem analysis either unsafe by re-executing effects or low-fidelity by losing execution context. We present DelAct, a tri-plane orchestration runtime that introduces a replayable boundary decoupling deliberation from actuation. DelAct comprises three cooperating planes: a control plane that maintains session state and orchestrates next steps without performing side effects; a data plane that routes all tool invocations through commitment-hash governance, binding each intent to a stable identifier for idempotent execution, in-doubt verification, and compensation rollback; and an observability plane that persists an append-only event log enabling deterministic replay and replay-to-live forking with lineage tracking. We evaluate DelAct on a Ticket/Invoice workflow under injected timeout and partial-failure faults. The results demonstrate that full governance eliminates timeout-induced duplicate writes and removes residual writes after failures (with duplicate/residual statistics aggregated over the E1 fault-injection runs), achieving a 66.5 ms mean rollback MTTR (Mean Time to Repair), while incurring predictable tail-latency overhead due to durable logging and governance checks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Biphasic Sketch: Multi-Attribute Stream Summarization for Arbitrary Attribute Combinations.
abstract: Sketch is a kind of memory efficient probabilistic data structure with error guarantees, which can realize realtime aggregation and approximate queries in data streams. The existing sketch mostly focuses on single attribute statistics, or only supports predefined multi-attribute combinations. Deviation from the predefined attribute combinations in a query requires additional refactoring overhead. Existing multi-attribute sketch solutions, such as OmniSketch and Hydra, still face the dual bottlenecks of limited update throughput and huge memory overhead in high speed data streaming scenarios. Therefore, we propose Biphasic Sketch (BS), a novel sketch that supports arbitrary attribute combination queries with theoretical error bounds, while featuring low memory overhead and high insertion throughput. BS utilizes HyperLogLog and MinHash, enabling element insertion in $O(s)$ time, where s is the number of attributes of an element. Under limited memory budgets, comprehensive experiments show that BS (including both the basic and advanced versions) achieves $1.5 \times$ the insertion throughput of state-of-theart sketches. Additionally, advanced BS achieves a $1.8 \times$ reduction in the estimation error on average.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Congestion-Resilient Auditable V2X Alert Scheduling with Publicly Checkable Evidence.
abstract: Cooperative V2X alert pipelines at RSUs must schedule time-critical warnings under bursty congestion and unreliable inputs, yet still support post-event scrutiny when raw logs are incomplete or cannot be fully disclosed. We design a congestion-resilient alert scheduler that keeps the online path lightweight while producing compact, publicly checkable evidence for later verification. The design (i) prioritizes alerts using an uncertainty-aware scheduling policy, (ii) enforces lightweight admissibility checks to filter malformed, stale, or inconsistent records, and (iii) anchors per-epoch evidence summaries to produce compact witnesses that enable third-party verification of decisions and blame attribution without requiring access to full private logs. We implement a log-driven replay evaluation that injects congestion stressors and adversarial invalid records, and compare against representative baselines under matched traces. The evaluation shows that CARVE preserves timeliness and robustness under congestion with bounded audit overhead: witness verification remains lightweight (logarithmic in the records per epoch), and the end-to-end pipeline adds only modest latency compared with scheduling-only baselines. Across congestion sweeps and invalid-input injections, we quantify the trade-off between tail latency and witness overhead, showing that CARVE contains P95/P99 delay while keeping witness verification cost small and predictable as the epoch size grows.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: PRO: Deterministic Load Balancing for AI Datacenter Network.
abstract: High-demand Large Language Model (LLM) services require high-bandwidth, scalable AI datacenter networks, where load balancing is critical to end-to-end applicationperceived communication performance. Existing datacenter network research primarily relies on randomized load balancing mechanisms to handle bursty, dynamic workloads. However, we argue that deterministic load balancing can be revitalized with significant potential, due to the synchronized traffic patterns and uniform packet size distributions inherent in LLM training workloads. In this paper, we propose PRO, a nearoptimal load balancing mechanism implemented on RDMA NICs. By orchestrating a deterministic round-robin order on RNICs with consideration of both intra-QP and inter-QP traffic, PRO realizes balanced queue distributions at both switch uplinks and downlinks. We implement a prototype of PRO using Intel FPGA NIC. Extensive evaluations show that PRO reduces 30% ~ 48% completion time (JCT) slowdown in the testbed, and up to 83.6% JCT slowdown compared to state-of-the-art DRILL, ConWeave, and Adaptive Routing.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RAPIDS: Reliable Adaptive Priority-based Intelligent Delivery Streaming for Enhanced Error Resilience in Real-time Video.
abstract: Real-time video streaming (RVS) has become the Internet’s dominant application, supporting latency-critical services from telemedicine to remote collaboration. However, stringent latency requirements force RVS systems to rely on UDP-based transport that tolerates packet loss, creating reliability challenges. Packet loss, whether from congestion or transmission errors, creates two irreconcilable failure modes: if corrupted reference frames are displayed, prediction errors propagate through all dependent frames, causing severe visual degradation; if packets are retransmitted aggressively, latency accumulates beyond real-time tolerances. This dilemma cannot be resolved within either layer independently: transport-layer mechanisms like retransmission or FEC exacerbate congestion, while codec-layer solutions like bitrate reduction degrade visual quality.We present RAPIDS, a codec-transport co-design that resolves this impasse through dynamic dependency restructuring. RAPIDS employs a deep reinforcement learning controller to adaptively designate frames as reference or non-reference based on real-time network conditions, effectively decoupling frame importance from encoding structure. This semantic information guides a partially reliable QUIC transport to implement differentiated protection: critical reference frames receive guaranteed delivery via retransmission, while non-reference frames can be proactively discarded under congestion to bound latency. Extensive evaluation on 1000+ real-world network traces demonstrates 28-50% QoS improvement over WebRTC, Salsify, and SODA, with a 4-5× faster error recovery during traffic bursts and network outages.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: StreamDuet: Bandwidth Efficient Multi-Drone Video Analytics with Iterative Streaming.
abstract: Drone video analytics is widely applied across various smart city services, including traffic monitoring, industrial inspection, and crowd anomaly detection. However, a single drone often suffers from occlusions and poor viewing angles, leading to significant accuracy reduction. Multi-drone systems capture videos from multiple perspectives, which enhance the accuracy by integrating complementary information from different fields of view (FoVs). Despite this advantage, limited bandwidth in drone networks makes it challenging to transmit high-resolution videos efficiently. This paper introduces StreamDuet, a system designed to enable high-accuracy and low-bandwidth video analytics in multi-drone systems. To this end, it addresses key challenges by leveraging three core components: 1) a Dynamic FoV Region of Interest (RoI) Prediction that quickly and accurately identifies accuracy-beneficial regions in each video chunk and encodes only them into video streams, 2) a Spatio-Temporal Inference Results Sharing mechanism that effectively manages and shares inference results across FoVs and continuous frames among multiple drones, and 3) a Temporal Robust Inference Results Reuse module that predicts current frame results by reusing inferences from previous frames within a single drone. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that StreamDuet improves $\mathbf{8}-\mathbf{4 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$ accuracy and reduces 28-61% bandwidth consumption compared to the state-of-the-art systems.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Switch-Transparent Load Balancing for RDMA Data Centers: A Host-Only Approach.
abstract: Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) equips modern data centers (DCs) with high-performance data transmission. Yet, its potential is often unmet, as the State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) RDMA traffic load balancers struggle to balance highperformance with practicability. In this paper, we first analyse existing RDMA-aware load balancers, examining their trade-offs across four key metrics: path utilization, packet order preservation, implementation overhead, and deployment complexity. We then present HP3, a host-based load balancer designed to excel in all these dimensions. HP3 combines Proactive Path Perception for real-time path state awareness with Reorder Free Rerouting to guarantee in-order packet delivery. It maintains low intrusiveness by complying with the standard RDMA transport layer and activating only during severe congestion. Implemented purely on end-hosts with no switch modifications, HP3 offers a practical solution with modest additional overhead. We prototype HP3 using DPDK and commodity RNICs, and evaluate it on a P4programmable switch testbed. Experiments with diverse data center workloads show that HP3 outperforms SOTA RDMA load balancers by up to $\mathbf{3 . 4} \times$ for typical traffic and $\mathbf{1 . 3} \times$ for AI training traffic.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: IntentVQA: A QoE-Aware Cloud-End Collaborative System for Video QA.
abstract: The proliferation of short-video platforms has catalyzed the demand for interactive Video Question Answering (Video QA), where users seek immediate, context-aware answers during playback. While Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) enable such interactivity, deploying them presents a fundamental resource dichotomy: cloud-based execution suffers from high latency and operational costs, whereas end-side resources are insufficient for heavy reasoning. Existing computation offloading schemes, typically driven by data size or bandwidth, fail to address the semantic heterogeneity of QA tasks, leading to suboptimal Quality of Experience (QoE). To bridge this gap, we propose IntentVQA, a cloud-end collaborative system that decouples reasoning capability from interaction latency. Unlike rigid offloading, IntentVQA introduces a semantic-aware hybrid execution framework. It dynamically orchestrates queries based on intent complexity-dispatching open-ended reasoning to the cloud while processing factual atomic tasks on the end side. To enable precise yet lightweight dispatching, we design a Semantic Router, which fuses textual embeddings with video profiles to predict the QoE utility of execution paths without heavy inference overhead. Furthermore, to resolve the semantic gap between flexible user queries and rigid end-side operators, we develop a Bidirectional Alignment Adapter. This module translates natural language into executable inputs and reconstructs raw outputs into conversational responses via a distillation-based generator. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IntentVQA significantly reduces interaction latency while maintaining high response accuracy, validating its effectiveness in optimizing QoE for interactive video streaming.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Scalable Simulation-based Configuration Verification of DCNs via Destination-Independent Compression.
abstract: Modern cloud data center networks (DCNs) often span tens of thousands of switches, challenging configuration verification, even for the state-of-the-art simulation-based configuration verification tools. While prior work has accelerated individual stages of the verification pipeline, these fragmented optimizations fall short of addressing the end-to-end scalability bottlenecks inherent in hyper-scale networks. To address this, we present sNetVeri, a scalable simulation-based configuration verifier for hyper-scale DCNs, built on the key insight that networks are often highly structured and compressible. Unlike prior compression methods tied to specific destinations, sNetVeri introduces a destination-independent one-shot compression strategy with formal correctness guarantees. sNetVeri further improves scalability through two designs: (1) a Dijkstra-based BGP simulation algorithm augmented with a withdrawal mechanism to support both monotonic and non-monotonic configurations, and (2) a highly parallel data-plane verification framework that operates directly on the shared compressed topology. Extensive evaluations on both production DCNs from Huawei Cloud and synthetic topologies demonstrate that sNetVeri scales efficiently to networks with over 10,000 switches while maintaining accuracy in controlplane simulation and data-plane verification.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: LARSS: A Hardware-Software Co-designed Framework for Load-Aware Receive Side Scaling.
abstract: In modern data centers, the widespread deployment of software network functions on multi-core servers demands efficient resource management to satisfy deterministic Service-Level Objectives (SLOs) while maximizing cost-effectiveness. However, skewed traffic and flow-affinity constraints render static provisioning inefficient. Existing adaptive scheduling schemes, typically categorized into proactive dispatching and reactive migration, face an inherent trade-off between responsiveness and management granularity. In this paper, we propose LARSS, a hardware-software co-designed framework that reconciles hardware-level agility with software intelligence. LARSS introduces a heterogeneity-aware load characterization model and augmented hardware primitives to facilitate seamless cross-layer coordination. We formalize workload migration as an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) problem and develop a lightweight heuristic to optimize load balancing with minimal migration frequency. Furthermore, LARSS employs an in-band signaling mechanism to ensure packet ordering and state consistency without prohibitive synchronization overheads. Experimental results from our FPGA-CPU prototype demonstrate that LARSS reduces the coefficient of variation (CV) of per-core loads by about $\mathbf{1 8} \boldsymbol{\%} \boldsymbol{5}^{\mathbf{5}} \boldsymbol{7} \boldsymbol{\%}$ compared to state-of-the-art solutions. This reduced load imbalance directly contributes to improved throughput and mitigated tail latency without the necessity of resource overprovisioning.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Fair Scheduling for Lossless RDMA Networks.
abstract: Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) is widely used in data centers for low latency, high throughput, and low CPU overhead. However, switch-side scheduling remains critical and challenging, as existing simple schedulers often lack fairness under high load or bursty traffic, while traditional fair scheduling relies on strict packet service order, limiting buffer flexibility and increasing packet-drop risk. This paper presents Relaxed-Order Fair Scheduling (ROFS), a switch-side fair scheduling mechanism for lossless RDMA networks. ROFS relaxes strict in-order packet service and adaptively controls per-flow packet admission to improve fairness under bounded reordering. It combines a fast-lane queue, regular scheduling queues, and stepwise threshold control to distribute packets across queues and reuse remaining buffer space, thereby reducing packet-drop risk. Receiver-side Selective Acknowledgment (SACK) distinguishes reordered packets from lost packets and avoids unnecessary retransmissions. Simulations show that ROFS reduces Flow Completion Time (FCT) by $\mathbf{5}-\mathbf{1 2} \times$ and improves fairness by $\mathbf{2}-\mathbf{5} \times$. ROFS can be deployed through an IRN-like RNIC/firmware extension or modern RoCE NICs supporting selective-repeat retransmission.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: AuEx: Automatic Exploration for Fresh Creative Ads via Large-Scale Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: With the extensive growth of short-video sharing platforms (SVSPs), it has become one of the most important platforms for Internet advertising. As more and more advertisers join SVSPs, the volume of fresh creative ads is also increasing dramatically. These fresh creative ads can not only affect the current revenue, but also play an important role in the accurate placement of subsequent history-rich ads. Through the analysis of real-world industrial data, we for the first time deeply discuss the current situation of fresh creative ads on SVSPs, as well as potential issues. With the unique features of ads on SVSPs, we propose a novel framework to enable fresh creative ads Automatic Exploration, namely AuEx, which is based on large-scale deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Via environmental feedbacks, the DRL-based AuEx can simultaneously optimize the revenue, user experience and pure exploration, rather than simply pursuing improvements on the one side of the road. AuEx has been deployed in a real-world SVSP environment, satisfying the online stability requirements and request time constraints. Compared with two online running exploration frameworks, experimental results have demonstrated that AuEx has simultaneously achieved significant improvements in terms of revenue, user experience, and pure exploration.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: DepartKVS: KV Separation for Redundant Replicas in Strongly Consistent Distributed Stores.
abstract: Distributed key-value (KV) stores ensure high availability and fault tolerance by maintaining data replicas across multiple servers. The conventional approach to managing replicas on each node stores multiple copies of KV pairs within the same index structure, which introduces significant read and write amplification. Recent work mitigates this overhead by employing separate index structures for primary replicas. However, redundant replicas within a node are still managed using uniform indexing, which degrades read and write performance, particularly under strong consistency constraints where multiple replicas must be accessed per operation. Leveraging the efficient random access performance of SSDs, we propose a KV separation design tailored for managing redundant replicas. Our approach decouples keys and values for redundant replicas by storing only keys in the two-layer log while relocating values larger than 4KB to a separate value log, thereby improving read and write performance and more effectively utilizing device bandwidth. To efficiently reclaim space from stale values, we introduce a lightweight garbage collection mechanism that operates incrementally and defers collection during background operations to minimize I/O interference. We further leverage SSD parallelism through asynchronous prefetching to optimize range query performance. We implement DepartKVS and conduct extensive experiments. Results demonstrate consistent performance gains across varying replica counts, data sizes, consistency levels, and garbage collection frequencies. Under the highest read and write consistency settings, DepartKVS improves read and update throughput by up to $1.92 \times$ and write throughput by up to $2.02 \times$, while reducing average read latency by 16-58% and 99th percentile read latency by $\mathbf{3 4}-\mathbf{6 6} \%$, and average update latency by 17-56% with 99th percentile reductions of 22-62%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SwitchNN: In-Network CNN Inference for Edge-Assisted Smart Roadside Networks.
abstract: As CNN inference becomes a dominant smart roadside workload, transmitting massive requests from distributed street-level cameras to resource-constrained edge servers creates severe queuing bottlenecks. Offloading partial CNN computations to programmable switches offers a promising path to scale compute. However, this faces two fundamental roadblocks: switches lack hardware primitives for complex arithmetic, and these early inference stages inherently inflate intermediate data by up to 20×, overwhelming network bandwidth. In this paper, we introduce SwitchNN, an in-network CNN inference architecture that resolves these bottlenecks. To alleviate bandwidth pressure, SwitchNN compresses intermediate features using Product Quantization. We propose an Operation Fusion technique that unifies the complex sequence of convolution and compression operations into a single, switch-friendly Index-to-Index Table lookup. Additionally, a tile-based iteration mechanism maximizes per-packet compute density strictly within physical hardware limits. Extensive evaluations on a Tofino switch demonstrate that SwitchNN reduces 99th-percentile queuing delay by up to 96% and improves maximum end-to-end goodput by up to $\mathbf{1 6} \times$ under strict SLAs, while maintaining a marginal 1-2% accuracy loss.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: PSM: Timely and Resource-Efficient Sketch Migration in Network Measurement.
abstract: Sketches can achieve resource-efficient and highaccurate network measurement (NM) with configurable resourceperformance trade-offs. Due to network dynamics, network measurement points (i.e., the switches deployed with sketches) need to reallocate dynamically to cover full traffic. However, using existing approaches to migrate sketches leads to unacceptable latency and resource overhead. In this paper, we propose PSM, a framework for timely and resource-efficient sketch migration. For timeliness, PSM utilizes a protocol that is able to access sketch counters and migrate them in parallel using background traffic. To ensure migration without direct traffic, we leverage programmable switches’ mirroring and recirculation functions to generate packets. For resource efficiency, PSM uses bitmap structures and hardware-friendly computations to track the migration progress and verify integrity. We implement PSM on Intel Tofino2 switches and compare PSM with three state-of-theart approaches through extensive experiments. Results indicate that PSM achieves timely and resource-efficient sketch migration.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: DP-MPC: Offloading Secure Multi-Party Computation to Programmable Data Planes.
abstract: With the growing demand for data privacy, secure multi-party computation (MPC) has been widely adopted across various applications. However, existing frameworks incur substantial communication overhead due to their inherently multi-round interactions and remain vulnerable to man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks. To address these limitations, this paper introduces DP-MPC, a framework that offloads MPC to the programmable data plane with low-overhead communication and lightweight security verification. Specifically, (1) we design a DP-MPC protocol that transforms multi-round MPC interactions into a single round of in-network aggregation, drastically reducing communication overhead; (2) we implement line-rate execution of three fundamental MPC operation types and maintain per-session state directly within the data plane pipeline, achieving high-performance MPC offloading; (3) we integrate a lightweight hash-based verification mechanism to proactively defend against MitM attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that DP-MPC reduces communication overhead by two orders of magnitude, achieves microsecond level end-to-end latency, and effectively mitigates MitM attacks.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SpecOffload: Unlocking Latent GPU Capacity for LLM Inference on Resource-Constrained Devices.
abstract: Efficient LLM inference on resource-constrained devices presents significant challenges in compute and memory utilization. Due to limited GPU memory, existing systems offload model weights to CPU memory, incurring substantial I/O overhead between the CPU and GPU. This leads to two major inefficiencies: (1) GPU cores are underutilized, often remaining idle while waiting for data to be loaded; and (2) GPU memory has low impact on performance, as reducing its capacity has minimal effect on overall throughput.In this paper, we propose SpecOffload, a high-throughput inference engine that embeds speculative decoding into offloading. Our key idea is to unlock latent GPU resources for storing and executing a draft model used for speculative decoding, thus accelerating inference at near-zero additional cost. To support this, we carefully orchestrate the interleaved execution of target and draft models in speculative decoding within the offloading pipeline, and propose a planner to manage tensor placement and select optimal parameters. Compared to the best baseline, SpecOffload improves GPU core utilization by 4.49x and boosts inference throughput by 2.54x. Our code is available at https://github.com/MobiSense/SpecOffload-public .
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Speak Your Network: Automated Network Emulation Construction with Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Orchestration.
abstract: Network research often relies on high fidelity emulation, but constructing greenfield environments still requires substantial manual effort. LLM agents face a gap between intent and implementation: long contexts, weak validation, and uniform model use make it difficult to translate intent into working emulator state. We present Nice, a closed-loop multi-agent framework that constructs greenfield emulations from natural language intents. Nice combines a hierarchical supervisor and worker architecture with context isolation, closed-loop verification for state grounding and self-healing, dual-layer experience memory, and adaptive LLM routing. On a 30-task benchmark, Nice increases success rate from 3.3% to 90.0%, reduces average model cost from ${\$}$0.045 to ${\$}$0.034 per task relative to the variant without routing, and improves first pass rate from 46.7% to 76.7%.
